payload.description:
Deterministic, token-free usage telemetry: count which terminal tools (rg, fd, bat, jq, yq, uv, ...) the agent actually invokes, so idle skills/tools can be culled from the catalog with real data. Requested 2026-07-16; design delegated and settled below after researching both platforms.

## Design
- New catalog hook script .basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py (stdlib only, never blocks: every path ends exit 0). Reads the hook JSON from stdin, accepts BOTH shapes: Claude Code PostToolUse (tool_name == Bash, tool_input.command) and Copilot postToolUse (toolName/tool_name in {bash, Bash, shell}, toolArgs/tool_input command field). Splits the command string on shell operators (pipes, &&, ||, ;, newlines), takes each segment head token, skips env assignments and shell builtins (cd, echo, exit, ...), normalizes to basename.
- Persistence: .basicly/usage/tool-usage.json mapping tool -> {count, last_used date}; atomic replace (tmp + os.replace), tolerant of a missing/corrupt file (restart from empty). The hook writes .basicly/usage/.gitignore containing '*' on first run (self-ignoring dir, like .beads) so the data survives sessions but never enters git. Per-repo-folder by design (worktrees accumulate their own).
- Claude wiring: hooks.yaml entry (id tool-usage, manager claude, stage posttooluse, matcher Bash). claude_settings.py currently hardcodes PreToolUse + the Edit|Write matcher — generalize: derive the settings event from the spec stage (pretooluse -> PreToolUse, posttooluse -> PostToolUse) and add an optional matcher field to hooks.yaml (default stays the current write-tools matcher).
- Copilot wiring: hooks live in .github/hooks/*.json ({"version": 1, "hooks": {"postToolUse": [{type command, bash/powershell/command keys, optional matcher}]}}). Add manager 'copilot' to HOOK_MANAGERS with a projection to .github/hooks/basicly-tool-usage.json (bash + powershell keys both run the same python script via uv), wired into hooks-build/hooks-check/uninstall like the claude manager.
- Dogfood: the hook ships in this repo's own projections (hooks-build here).

## Non-functional
- Zero tokens: pure python, no model calls. Resilient: never fails the tool call (async-safe, exit 0 always), atomic writes, corrupt-file recovery. Survives sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Piping a recorded Claude PostToolUse Bash JSON into the script increments counts for each pipeline segment head (e.g. 'rg foo | jq .x' -> rg+1, jq+1) and writes the self-ignoring .gitignore
- The Copilot stdin shape is parsed by the same script (unit test with both payload shapes)
- A corrupt or missing usage file never fails the hook (exit 0) and the next write starts clean
- hooks-build projects the Claude PostToolUse group into .claude/settings.json and the Copilot hook file into .github/hooks/, both idempotent; hooks-check flags drift; uninstall removes both
- Existing pretooluse protect-generated behavior is unchanged (matcher default preserved)
- Dogfooded: this repo's projections carry the hook after hooks-build; git status stays clean after a counted command runs
- Regression tests cover parsing, counting, atomicity fallback, both stdin shapes, and both projections
payload.title: Tool-usage counting hook projected to Claude and Copilot

## Steps to Reproduce

Run basicly board --out on this repository: 15.8 s, 28 percent of the local suite in one test; profiled to an un-memoised policy.session_issue_ids walk costing 5.9 s per beat, re-derived for every beat of one build.

- Given one board build when session_issue_ids is needed by several beats then the walk over the ledger is performed at most once per build
- Given the existing board tests when the memoisation lands then they pass unchanged and the board --out consumer test drops measurably in wall time
- Given two consecutive builds when the ledger changed between them then the second build reflects the change (no cross-build staleness)

- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_snapshot.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-b9ef` landed a gate for a stale claim in an **epic's** problem statement, because a
decider reads that text as fact. The same failure exists one level up and nothing checks it: a
requirements document is read as fact by every human and agent that plans from it, and four of
its current claims are false against the tree. Each was verified 2026-08-13.

**1. `factory-loop.md:358-363` - "All seven are authored and dispatched as of 2026-08-09. The
gap this section had measured since 2026-08-08 - 'the projection works and nothing consumes it'
- is closed."**

Refuted. **0 of 346 recorded dispatch commands contain `--agent`**, against a positive control
of 163 containing `-p`. `resolve_role` has exactly one call site (`loop.py:745`) and the
supervised lane path passes no role at all (`rg role src/basicly/supervise.py` returns zero
hits). `implementation-plan.md:112-124` already carries the correction; this document does not,
and it is the document the roster work plans against.

**2. `factory-loop.md:404-407` - "`skills:` preloads a skill's full body at subagent startup."**

Half true, and the false half is the one that matters. Probed twice on claude 2.1.231 with a
positive control: preload happens for a definition **spawned as a subagent**, and does **not**
happen under `claude --agent <name> -p`, which is this repo's only dispatch shape. Five agent
definitions declare `skills:` and get nothing from it. Owned by `basicly-ey58`; the document
still states the unqualified claim.

**3. `implementation-plan.md:225` - xjd2's "open question is answered twice over ... a competing
harness runs exactly this split in production, host-runtime dispatch for the same vendor."**

The cited section says the opposite. `factory-loop.md:1115` records that harness's loop as
"**prompt assembly**: the verbs 'do NOT call any LLM', they emit a prompt to stdout. The loop is
prose in `SKILL.md` the model executes." That is an existence proof for the *re-scope* branch of
`basicly-xjd2`, not for engine-driven host dispatch. The row's justification therefore does not
support the row.

**4. `implementation-plan.md:132-135` - "validator, reviewer, retrospector and curator resolve
correctly today and can never be invoked."**

`roles.py:63-71 ROLE_BY_PHASE` has **no `reviewer` entry at all**, so `reviewer` does not
resolve; and `curator` maps to `ship`, which **is** a live phase with a live handler - it is
unreachable only because `_on_ship` (`loop.py:441`) never calls `_run_agent`. So the count and
the reason are both wrong. `basicly-u2hl.54`'s comment 2085 recorded this correction and the
plan never absorbed it.

Also unamended and already known false: `factory-loop.md:1163-1165` (section 12 / D6) still
carries "Context | one window shared by everything" and "The last row is why light cannot
replace dark", which D24 (`:100`) concedes architecture section 5 records as **isolated**.

**5. `factory-loop.md` section 15.5 asserts a defect that no longer exists.**

It reads "`runner_usage.claude_json_usage` never populates `cache_read_tokens`/
`cache_write_tokens` ... **0 of 297 dispatch records carry a cache split**". `basicly-i4gg`
landed the split on 2026-08-13 (`_claude_usage_split`, `runner_usage.py:201`, cited by bead id
in its own docstring) and shipped. Leaving the section as written arms exactly the failure mode
section 5.2 row 5 describes: a reader plans against a defect that was fixed.

**6. The document contradicts itself about the context ceiling, and a bead cannot be written
until one side wins.**

- `:1308` (section 15.6): "The context ceiling is **deleted, not retuned**."
- `:99` (D23, later and general): "**A sizing control with no recorded correct firing becomes
  observability** ... the runner timeout, the working-set band and the **context ceiling** have
  zero between them ... **Demotion is not deletion: the number stays recorded, surfaced and
  falsifiable**, because section 15.6's gate was wrong for months with the telemetry already
  contradicting it."

D23 names the context ceiling explicitly and postdates 15.6, so it should win - but
`basicly-u2hl.30`'s acceptance criterion is written to the 15.6 half and demands the constant,
its meter and its follow-up path be **absent**. A lane implementing it as written deletes a
number D23 requires kept. This is an owner decision, not a wording fix, and `basicly-89hm` now
depends on `u2hl.30`, so it blocks the context-window work too.

## The general defect, which is the reason this is one bead and not four

A committed requirements claim has no falsifiability gate. `docs-claims` checks generated
blocks; `corpus-drift` checks an epic's `## Context` bullets against its own closed children.
Neither reads a requirements document. So a decision recorded on 2026-08-09 can be refuted by
2026-08-11's code and the document keeps asserting it, which is how a session plans a P0 against
a remedy the plan replaced - measured today on `basicly-89hm`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n "All seven are authored and dispatched" docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`

## Measured
`gh run list --workflow=quality-gates.yml --limit 40`, read 2026-09-12:

- 39 completed runs
- 13 failures
- **33 percent**, one run in three

Every failure is the same job and the same step: `Quality gates on windows-latest`, in `Run full checks (ruff, format, pyright, bandit, pytest)`. In each of those runs the ubuntu and macos jobs passed. The failures span 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-12, so this is not a recent regression.

## The one instance still in the logs
Run 34716451926 on 4534b1e2:

```
assert outcome.result.returncode == 0, outcome.detail
AssertionError: runner exited 1
tests/test_integration_loop.py::test_a_supervisor_pass_runs_two_agent_processes_and_lands_both
```

A standin runner subprocess exited 1 under `D:/a/basicly/basicly/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`. The whole diff of that commit was a version string, a changelog fragment and the ledger, with zero files under `src/` or `tests/`, so the commit cannot be causal.

Logs for the older failures have expired, so I cannot say whether all thirteen are this test. That is the first thing to find out.

## Why it matters
A gate that fails a third of the time is not a gate. It trains everyone to re-run rather than read, and a real windows regression would arrive looking exactly like the noise. The repository ships to windows, linux and macos, and only one of the three is unreliable in CI.

## First step
Keep the failing artefacts. The step should upload the pytest output and the runner stdout and stderr on failure, so the next occurrence is diagnosable instead of expired. Then decide from three or four captured instances whether it is one test or several.

## Owner note
The owner said the windows gate "fails often" before this was measured. It does.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly session start` (basicly-askx4j) prints the ready set, the blocked set, the live grants and the decision targets, every line derived. It does not print where the last session stopped. That fact lives in the ledger as a note tagged `[session handover <date>]` on the root the session worked (the last one is on basicly-hnnmk9), and the gitignored `HANDOVER.md` existed only to point at that note and at the command. D-42 retires the file; the parent epic's acceptance line says `rg -l 'HANDOVER.md' --glob '!.basicly/ledger/**'` prints nothing when the epic closes. The `.gitignore` still names the file, so the acceptance line fails today.

The producer side has no rule either: the `session-finish` skill asks for a pickup-clean handoff summary but does not say where it is written, which is how the file came back after every session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly session start` runs against a ledger holding one or more notes whose text starts with `[session handover`, IT SHALL print the newest one first, with the record it sits on and the note text, and the `--json` payload SHALL carry it under `handover`.
- WHEN no record carries such a note, IT SHALL say so in one line and draw no table.
- WHEN `rg -l 'HANDOVER.md' --glob '!.basicly/ledger/**' --glob '!CHANGELOG.md'` runs after this lands, IT SHALL print nothing, against a positive control that finds `session start` in `src/basicly/cli.py`; `HANDOVER.md` is deleted from the working tree and from `.gitignore`.
- WHEN the `session-finish` skill is read, IT SHALL say the handover is written as a `[session handover <date>]` note on the root record through `basicly tracker write -- comments add`, never as a file.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_session.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/session-finish/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/**`
- `.gitignore`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly session start` prints a `Handover` line naming basicly-hnnmk9 before the ready set; `rg -l 'HANDOVER.md' --glob '!.basicly/ledger/**' --glob '!CHANGELOG.md'` prints nothing.

payload.text: [research findings 2026-10-31] Recommendation: WAIT (hold); retain the current adapters. Upstream ai is explicitly beta and maps provider event names to ordinary lefthook run hook commands at install time (https://lefthook.dev/configuration/ai/). Supported providers are Claude, Codex, Cursor and Copilot. Inspected shipped v2.2.2 source from https://codeload.github.com/evilmartians/lefthook/tar.gz/refs/tags/v2.2.2, archive SHA256 c635447bcdb0b9f731e4ae54ac842c222ac6932bd545f87fe48fc20818b4c5f6: internal/command/install.go calls validateAIHooks/installAIHooks, uninstall.go calls uninstallAIHooks; internal/config/ai.go defines provider maps. Both shipped LICENSE copies are MIT (2019 Arkweid), matching basicly's retained license. Bounded binary experiment with .basicly/bin/lefthook version 2.2.2 in disposable repositories seeded a foreign entry in each provider file, ran install, the generated command, then uninstall. Claude/Codex/Cursor preserved foreign entries through install and uninstall; Copilot overwrote its same-file entry and deleted lefthook.json on uninstall while preserving a separate consumer.json. All generated commands used plain lefthook run audit, with no machine-specific binary path. A job exiting 2 made the exact generated command return 1, including without --force. Current Claude docs distinguish blocking exit 2 from nonblocking other errors (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Independent upstream report https://github.com/evilmartians/lefthook/issues/1511 remains open and reproduces that loss. payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly loop supervise basicly-zq9i2m --tier high --max-passes 8`. Passes 4 to 8 were identical: `carried: basicly-2kh170 - landing without a new dispatch`, then `routed: basicly-2kh170 -> rework` on the same scope collision, then the pass spend gate refused (`89259646 tokens forecast; 87452222 remaining`), then `decider: basicly-zq9i2m#3018546b66 [escalation] to human` with a fresh decider rendering each time. The ledger holds 5 `[harness-run] phase=decide` records for that one decision id. Nothing changed between the passes: no lane dispatched, no landing succeeded, the queue held the same item. The session ended `stopped: --max-passes 8 reached`, so five of eight passes bought nothing and the operator read a full pass count as work.

Two defects share the root that a pass has no notion of "this pass changed nothing":

1. `record_pass_refusal` is idempotent per (issue, kind, question), so the queue item was correctly re-enqueued once, but the decider was dispatched again on every pass for an item it had already routed to a human. A human-routed item is pending until a human answers; re-deciding it spends a decider run per pass and cannot change the answer.
2. A pass whose only outcomes are a repeated landing refusal and a repeated queue item is a stall. The supervisor kept looping until `--max-passes`, and a session without that flag would loop until the operator noticed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Root with one carried lane whose landing bounces on a stable cause (a scope collision with a live sibling), and ready children whose forecast exceeds the remaining grant. `basicly loop supervise <root> --max-passes 4`. Observed: 4 identical passes, 4 decider runs on one decision id. Expected: after the first pass that changes nothing, the session ends with a `stalled:` narrative naming the pending decision and the bounced lane, and the decider runs at most once per queue item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a queue item the decider already routed to a human when the next pass finds it still pending then no decider dispatch runs for it and the pass narrative names it as `pending (human)`.
- Given a pass that dispatched no lane, landed no lane and enqueued no new item when the pass ends then the supervisor ends the session with `stalled:` naming every pending item and bounced lane, and exits non-zero.
- Given a pass that dispatched or landed at least one lane then the session continues as today.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_supervise.py -q` with a test that drives two identical no-progress passes through the supervisor and asserts one decider dispatch and a `stalled:` ending.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14 and reproduced by hand.

```python
# src/basicly/loader.py:191
def _infer_source_from_path(path: Path) -> str:
    parts = {part.lower() for part in path.parts}
    if ".basicly-local" in parts or "user" in parts:
        return "user"
    return "core"
```

`path` is absolute. Reproduced:

```text
<redacted:posix-home-path>   core
<redacted:posix-home-path>            user
<redacted:posix-home-path>               user
<redacted:posix-absolute-path>                 user
```

The lowercase fold makes `User` match too.

## Which root reaches it

`cli._fragment_roots` (cli.py:201-205) passes `None` as the source hint for the legacy root `paths.legacy_fragments_dir`. Any fragment loaded from there infers its source from the path. That root is absent in this repository, so the defect does not fire here. It fires in a consumer repository that still carries it, on a machine whose home directory is named user.

## What a wrong provenance permits

Provenance selects real semantics, both verified:

- `loader._validate_replacements` (loader.py:107-118) downgrades a `ValidationError` to a warning when `fragment.source == "user"`. A `replaces` that names an unknown id stops being an error.
- `planner._apply_user_replacements` (planner.py:132-147) drops any core fragment that a user fragment names in `replaces`.

So on such a checkout a fragment can silently remove an always-on rule from every agent in that repository.

## Why this repository forbids it

Behaviour varies by the absolute path of the checkout. The portability rule states that no committed artifact may depend on a machine path, and this is the same defect one layer in: the code reads the machine path at run time.

## Acceptance

- While a fragment loads from a root with no source hint, then the loader infers `user` only from the overlay marker directory, or from a component relative to the fragment root, and never from the absolute prefix of the checkout.
- When the loader runs against a fixture rooted under a path containing `user`, then it infers `core`.
- A regression test ships with the fix.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loader.py`
- `tests/test_loader.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_loader.py -q` with a fixture rooted under a temporary path that contains a `user` component.
payload.title: fragment provenance reads any path component named user as an overlay

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-08-26, watching the wall during the basicly-zq9i2m pass: "i see no indicator on the board that something is happening ... It is impossible for the user to understand what is happening and why we are waiting." Measured at that moment from the snapshot and the supervisor log: 2 lanes had landed, 3 lanes had finished and sat in the serial landing queue, one landing was running (rebase, full verify, merge, 3-8 minutes), and 1 lane had been refused by the WIP bound with 0 units past build. Every card read `build`, `not confirmed live`, dotted border. The producer knows all four facts (`dispatch: ... finished; ready to land`, the landing it is running, `wip: ... REFUSED: basicly-oqspon`) and publishes none of them; the snapshot lane has `live` true or false and nothing between.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's agent has exited with work committed and the lane waits for the merge queue, THE CARD SHALL say `waits to land` with its queue position, not `build` and `not confirmed live`.
- WHEN the supervisor runs a landing, THE BOARD SHALL show which lane lands now, the stage it is in (rebase, verify, merge, tracker commit) and how long that stage has run, refreshed on every tick.
- WHEN a ready lane was refused at admission (WIP bound, spend ceiling, band), THE CARD SHALL carry the refusal and its reason in place, and SHALL NOT render as an idle build.
- WHEN nothing is running and nothing is landing, THE BOARD SHALL say what the pass waits for (a human checkpoint, a blocker record, the next pass) in one sentence at the top.
- WHERE a fact is not on the snapshot contract, THE SCHEMA SHALL gain the field (`lane.state` as a closed set: `queued`, `running`, `waits-to-land`, `landing`, `refused`, `parked`) and the producer SHALL write it; the consumer SHALL render it with the word plus the colour plus the border, no glyph.
- Demonstrated by: run a pass with more ready lanes than the WIP bound admits, read the wall while a landing runs, and confirm all four states are named on the page.

## Scope

payload.title: the board has no state between running and idle so a finished lane a running landing and a refused lane all read as nothing happening

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Owner, 2026-08-26, watching the wall during the basicly-zq9i2m pass: "i see no indicator on the board that something is happening ... It is impossible for the user to understand what is happening and why we are waiting." Measured at that moment from the snapshot and the supervisor log: 2 lanes had landed, 3 lanes had finished and sat in the serial landing queue, one landing was running (rebase, full verify, merge, 3-8 minutes), and 1 lane had been refused by the WIP bound with 0 units past build. Every card read `build`, `not confirmed live`, dotted border. The producer knows all four facts (`dispatch: ... finished; ready to land`, the landing it is running, `wip: ... REFUSED: basicly-oqspon`) and publishes none of them; the snapshot lane has `live` true or false and nothing between.

## Steps to Reproduce

Start `basicly loop supervise <epic>` over six ready children with `[policy] max_downstream_wip = 5`, open `basicly board serve`, and wait until the agents exit. Observed: five cards read `build` with a dotted border and no figure changes, one card holds an id and a phase only, and the page names no landing. Expected: three cards read `waits to land` with a queue position, one reads `landing: verify, 2m10s`, one reads `refused: WIP bound, 0 past build`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's agent has exited with work committed and the lane waits for the merge queue, THE CARD SHALL say `waits to land` with its queue position, not `build` and `not confirmed live`.
- WHEN the supervisor runs a landing, THE BOARD SHALL show which lane lands now, the stage it is in (rebase, verify, merge, tracker commit) and how long that stage has run, refreshed on every tick.
- WHEN a ready lane was refused at admission (WIP bound, spend ceiling, band), THE CARD SHALL carry the refusal and its reason in place, and SHALL NOT render as an idle build.
- WHEN nothing is running and nothing is landing, THE BOARD SHALL say what the pass waits for (a human checkpoint, a blocker record, the next pass) in one sentence at the top.
- WHERE a fact is not on the snapshot contract, THE SCHEMA SHALL gain the field (`lane.state` as a closed set: `queued`, `running`, `waits-to-land`, `landing`, `refused`, `parked`) and the producer SHALL write it; the consumer SHALL render it with the word plus the colour plus the border, no glyph.
- Demonstrated by: run a pass with more ready lanes than the WIP bound admits, read the wall while a landing runs, and confirm all four states are named on the page.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_supervise_board.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`

A full-suite bisect without that file passed them. Fixed by 8dfeb897, which drives the kit through subprocesses.

## Scope note
A blanket refusal of 'from tests.' does not fit: 238 test files import other test modules and pass. The trigger here was a test in the tests/test_git_hooks/ subpackage importing a top-level test module that loads kit modules with spec_from_file_location. The exact mechanism is not proven. The test-discipline skill does not cover it.

## Proposed control
Find the mechanism first, then gate it: for example a conftest check that fails a worker when a kit module name in sys.modules is replaced by a second load. Not claimed and not built.
Why merged: Fixed case by 8dfeb897; the remaining guard (fail on a second kit-module load per worker) is a small test-isolation check.

payload.description:
## Context

Found landing `basicly-e2mz.49`. Its new gate calls `ratchet.compose_ratchet(repo, "code_citations", ...)`,
which reads a `[ratchet.code_citations]` table from a `basicly.d` drop in. The config validator refuses
that section:

```
unknown section 'code_citations' in [ratchet]; [ratchet] accepts comment_density, module_size, noqa_debt
```

So the gate ships green and **can never be rebaselined by a lane**, which is the one route the gate's
own remedy text tells a lane to take. It failed 166 tests the moment a drop in used it. The gate was
green at merge because nobody exercised its rebaseline path - the recurring shape here is that a closed
record proves code exists, not that a route works.

The general control is the point of this record: **every gate name passed to `compose_ratchet` must be
registered in the config schema's accepted `[ratchet]` set**, bound by a test rather than by review.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add `[ratchet.code_citations]` with any key to a `basicly.d/<id>.toml`.
2. Run `uv run pytest -q`.
3. Observe a ValueError from `config.py` naming the section, and a broad test failure rather than a single one.
4. Observe that `[ratchet.module_size]` in the same file is accepted, which is the positive control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given every gate that calls compose_ratchet when the config schema is read then each gate name is in the accepted ratchet section set - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_config.py -k ratchet_sections -q`
- Given a gate name absent from that set then the test names the gate and the file that must declare it

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_config.py -k ratchet_sections -q`

## Trigger

When an early verification check has already failed, I want the harness to stop subsequent work under an explicit fail-fast setting, so feature development does not wait for expensive tests whose passing result cannot make this run pass.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/verify_artifact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/check_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
- `tests/test_verify_fail_fast.py`
- `tests/test_verify_artifact.py`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_check_runner.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`
- `docs/how-to/wire-up-the-verify-gate.md`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

## Design

Add a validated boolean verify.fail_fast setting, default false, and explicitly enable it for basicly in a task fragment. Preserve configured order, existing affected and staged snapshot boundaries, and every required check on the passing path. Both the engine and no-engine portable runner must stop after an actual failed check, name remaining selected checks as not run, preserve failure, and never mint successful cache receipts for incomplete work. Retry and landing diagnostics must retain incomplete coverage and cannot claim success from the failed check alone. Do not introduce parallelism, affected selection, new dependencies or test-result caching.

## Demonstration

Run the installed candidate wheel and native Lefthook pre-push against a consumer with a cheap failing check followed by an observable expensive check. Show the later marker absent with fail-fast true, present with default or false, and present after a passing first check. Measure elapsed time with the same bounded expensive fixture for each mode; report this as fixture evidence, not a general repository speed claim. Exercise a recovered first check and a still-failing retry to prove remaining work never vanishes from the verdict.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a legitimate withdrawal leaves later generations of the same fact, I want scrubbing and new writes to preserve event identity, so I can commit safe withdrawals without corrupting their audit history.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a scratch ledger, append a comment twice with distinct generations. Withdraw the generation-one event. Standalone fsck remains clean. Engine tracker.scrub_ledger refuses the surviving generation-two event because it derives densely from surviving payload counts. Recurrence then chooses generation one again, reusing the retired identifier; append produces withdrawal-resurrected. This behavior is also recorded in the closed basicly-vkh0.34 release artifact. The specialist searched folded record descriptions and comments with the known withdrawal card as positive control and found no open exact owner.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/fsck.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/recurrence.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_scrub_generations.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_withdrawal_generations.py`

## Repair Boundary

Reuse the existing bounded kit generation validation rather than introducing another inference rule. Preserve unchanged identifiers. Reserve surviving and retired identifiers when allocating changed payloads or repeats. Direct append must refuse a retired identifier. Preserve distinct events when redaction merges payloads. Do not rewrite the live ledger during tests.
payload.requirements: Keep bounded evidence-ID validation authoritative in one kit rule. Preserve all events, withdrawal audits, legitimate repeat semantics, standalone Python floor and existing integrity gates.
payload.title: Preserve event identities after withdrawal and ledger scrubbing

payload.description: Reported by the burndown-chart consumer: a 52-byte uv.lock appeared at their repo root after install, named by no install output, in a repo that is pip plus pip-compile and not uv managed. Reproduced here with a positive control - a scratch consumer repo carrying a pyproject.toml, install, then one commit: uv.lock appears with version = 1, revision = 3, requires-python = >=3.14, byte-identical in shape to theirs, and protect-generated-commit then fails with files were modified by this hook. Cause: every projected hook entry is uv run python <script> (precommit_config._hook_entry and hooks._copilot_hook_config), and uv run treats any directory with a pyproject.toml as a project, resolving and writing a lock. Every hook script is stdlib only plus sibling imports, so --no-project is safe; pipe-status-guard.py in this repo already uses that form.

payload.description: Verified live on 0.12.0: a repo with a hand-written .github/copilot-instructions.md ran basicly install and the file was replaced with the generated projection. No warning, no backup, and the previous content is unrecoverable. On a first install there is no manifest entry, so install cannot distinguish its own stale output from a file it has never seen, and it does not try. Reported as a question by a consumer preparing a first install with 273 lines in that file. AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md are the same shape. install --overwrite-scaffolds already writes a .basicly-bak sibling for scaffolds; the same treatment for an unrecognised file at a managed output path would close this.
payload.title: install silently destroys a hand-authored agent instructions file

payload.text: Proposed fix from the consumer session that reported it, and it is better than treating this as a manifest problem: on first install, when a build target path already exists and carries no manifest entry, write the existing bytes to <path>.basicly-bak before overwriting. That reuses the convention --overwrite-scaffolds already established rather than inventing one, and it sidesteps the hard part entirely - install never has to distinguish its own stale output from user content, because the distinction stops mattering once the bytes survive either way. Acceptance should cover the three always-on outputs (.github/copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md) and assert no backup is written on a repeat install, so the tree does not accumulate one per run.

## Trigger

When `src/basicly/repair_brief.py` and the `repair-in-place` skill both tell an agent how to repair in place and can drift apart, I want one source of truth between them, so I can trust the brief an implementer reads.

to repair in place. They say the same thing to the same reader.

The implementer agent gets both: the skill via its `skills:` frontmatter, the brief via the

being the one actually rendered into the prompt - is the copy that wins.

Verified 2026-08-13: `repair_brief.py` contains no reference to the skill.

## Proposed check

One source of truth. Either the brief is generated from the skill body or the skill is
reduced to what the brief cannot carry, with a test asserting the two cannot diverge.

[merged from basicly-jr0l.48, triage 2026-11-17] Review the phase ladder for accidental complexity without moving it to data
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When `derive_phase` drives a five-rung ladder over five inputs and a simpler engine drives a longer lifecycle elsewhere, I want each rung's predicate reviewed for accidental complexity, so I can justify or remove it without weakening the landed invariant.

## Context

From the Symphony analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/symphony.md`), kept as a separate concern
after declarative phases were rejected on 2026-07-30.

Symphony's engine knows only **three** predicates about a work item - active, terminal, neither - and
drives a seven-stage lifecycle on that alone. Our `derive_phase`
(`src/basicly/loop_state.py:106-143`) uses a five-rung ladder over five inputs: status, approved
checkpoints, worktree binding, gate status, and has-children.

The point is not to copy their model - they pay for that simplicity by holding all real state in RAM,
which is why the same analysis rejects their state design outright. The point is that a much simpler
engine drove a longer lifecycle, which is grounds to check ours for accidental complexity rather than
essential complexity.

Specific questions to answer, with the answer "it is all essential" being an acceptable and useful
outcome:

- Is `has_children` doing work that the worktree binding or the gate status does not already imply?
- Do `classify` and `decompose` need separate rungs, given both are checkpoint-gated and the
  decompose rung already ORs in `has_children`?
- Could the ladder be expressed as one ordered table of `(phase, predicate)` pairs where every
  predicate is a named function, making each independently testable? That keeps everything typed -
  it is a refactor for reviewability, explicitly *not* the rejected move to data.

Hard constraint: the `verified`/landed term must survive intact. It encodes the invariant from
incident `basicly-k35r` and is the reason declarative phases were rejected; a simplification that
loses it is a regression, not a simplification. Any change here needs the existing derive_ph
Why merged: derive_phase still at src/basicly/loop_state.py:75; a P3 review chore whose answer depends on which loop survives consolidation.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a committed non-manual runner default when an operator drives basicly loop run or basicly loop advance interactively then a documented per-invocation override restores the manual handoff without editing any committed or gitignored config
payload.close_reason: done
payload.description:
## Problem

`--runner` and `--autonomy` exist only on `basicly loop supervise`. `basicly loop run` and
`basicly loop advance` accept neither, so the runner cannot be chosen per invocation on the
single-track path — the committed `[runner] default` is the only answer available to it.

That forces one committed key to serve two incompatible modes. Autonomous mode wants a real
headless agent so a supervised pass dispatches at all. Interactive mode wants the `manual`
handoff, because the driving agent is already in the worktree and a build-phase dispatch
re-implements the node in a second process. There is no per-invocation escape on the
interactive path, so the only way to hold both is a gitignored `basicly.local.toml` override —
which is precisely what this repo does today, and why the committed default reads `manual` with
a comment explaining that autonomous dispatch would double-run the loop.

The consequence is that the committed default cannot express the product's intent. A repo that
wants supervised runs must either commit a default that sabotages its own interactive sessions,
or keep the real default in an uncommitted file no consumer inherits.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly loop supervise --help   # shows --runner and --autonomy
uv run basicly loop run --help         # shows neither
uv run basicly loop advance --help     # shows neither
```

Observed - `_apply_session_overrides` in `src/basicly/cli.py` is called only from
`_cmd_loop_supervise`; `loop run` and `loop advance` have no equivalent, so both read
`[runner] default` through `load_runner_config` with no override seam. With
`[runner] default = "claude"` committed, an interactive `basicly loop run <id>` at build phase
dispatches a headless agent and there is no flag that restores the handoff.

Expected - the runner and autonomy overrides are available on every path that can dispatch, so
a committed default that suits supervised runs does not have to be countermanded by an
uncommitted file to keep interactive driving usable.

## Scope

- src/basicly/cli.py
- tests/test_cli.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a committed non-manual `[runner] default` when an operator drives `basicly loop run` or
  `basicly loop advance` interactively then a documented per-invocation override restores the
  manual handoff without editing any committed or gitignored config
payload.title: Only loop supervise can override the runner so one committed default must serve two incompatible modes

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-20. `basicly-gvlpxm` and `basicly-kjc5.63` branched from the same commit. Both measured
`src/basicly/merge.py` and both found **exactly 2 tokens** of module size headroom. gvlpxm declared a
+79 rebaseline and spent that 2; kjc5.63 declared +190 against the same 15401 baseline and spent it
again. Composed on the rebase the module reads 15672 against a frozen 15401 + 79 + 190 = 15670, so the
gate refused by 2 and `test_check_module_size` failed with it.

Both lanes were green on their own branches. The failure exists only in the merge, and the operator sees
a two token overrun with no hint that two independently correct measurements caused it.

**A headroom figure is only valid against the tree it was taken on.** A drop in that recorded the base
commit its measurement was taken at could be refused when that commit is no longer an ancestor of the
head it is being applied to - which is a mechanical check, not a judgment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take two records whose scopes both include one module frozen near its baseline.
2. Dispatch both from the same base commit.
3. Have each measure the module's headroom and declare a rebaseline that fits.
4. Land the first; observe green.
5. Rebase and land the second; observe the module size gate refuse by the headroom both lanes spent, and the gate's own test fail with it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ratchet drop in that records the base commit of its measurement when it is applied to a head that commit is not an ancestor of then the gate refuses naming the stale measurement - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_dropin.py -k stale_measurement -q`
- Given a drop in whose recorded base is an ancestor of the head then it applies unchanged so existing drop ins keep working

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dropin.py`
- `tests/test_dropin.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/dropin.py`
- `tests/test_dropin.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_dropin.py -k stale_measurement -q`
payload.title: two lanes can each spend the last tokens of one module headroom and turn a green branch red on the merge

payload.close_reason: shipped by the harness loop
payload.description:
## Context

`basicly loop supervise` runs `while True` (`cli.py:3265`) and returns only when
`state.done` — every child of the root closed. There is no `--once`, no pass limit and no
stop command. Measured 2026-08-08 on session `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`: the root had 21 open
children and a 300,000,000-token grant, so the loop was committed to spending the whole
grant with no operator control short of a signal.

**Lock takeover is not the stop control it looks like.** `supervise.acquire`
(`supervise.py:159`) steals a lock only when the holder's heartbeat is older than
`STALE_AFTER_S`, and a healthy supervisor beats continuously. Takeover is crash recovery;
a working supervisor cannot be handed over or asked to finish.

So the only available lever is a signal to the process, and that is exactly the action the
repo's own cost rule forbids: **cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by interrupting a
working agent**. When this was hit, three lanes were mid-dispatch at 16.4M, 18.2M and 8.3M
tokens — roughly \$40 of work that a stop would have discarded — and two further lanes had
just been unblocked and would have been stranded with live worktrees.

## Why a signal is not good enough even when it is safe

The lanes are `claude -p` subprocesses of the supervisor. A signal to the parent leaves
their disposition unspecified: killed mid-write, or orphaned and still spending against a
grant nothing is now metering. Neither is a documented outcome, and the operator has to
pick the moment by watching a log, which is the manual polling this harness exists to
remove.

## Shape

The beat callback already exists for precisely this kind of prompt interrupt — `hb.check()`
runs once per pass and raises when ownership is lost, and the dispatcher takes a `beat`
callback "so a takeover stops the pass promptly" (`supervise.py:265`). The stop wants the
same path: a sentinel the beat reads, so the supervisor finishes the round it is in —
landing everything already dispatched — and then returns instead of seeding another.

A pass bound (`--max-passes`) is the cheaper half and worth having as well, because it lets
an operator commit to a bounded spend at launch rather than having to intervene at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a supervisor with lanes in flight, when an operator requests a stop, then the
  current round completes and every dispatched lane lands before the process returns, and
  no further lanes are seeded — check: a test starts a session with a stubbed runner,
  requests a stop mid-round, and asserts every in-flight lane reached a terminal route and
  the next round seeded zero lanes.
- Given `--max-passes N`, when the Nth pass completes, then the supervisor returns even
  with open children remaining — check: a test with two open children and `--max-passes 1`
  asserts one pass ran and the process returned non-zero with the reason named.
- Given a stop request, when the operator inspects the session afterwards, then the reason
  and who asked is recorded — check: a test asserts the stop writes a marker naming the
  requester.

## Demonstration

`basicly loop stop basicly-u2hl` (or the equivalent surface) prints the lanes it is waiting
to land, then returns after they land; `basicly worktree list` shows no orphaned worktree
and `basicly loop status` on each lane shows a terminal phase rather than a live dispatch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop.skill.yaml`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the working set band when its maximum is resolved for a pass then it is bounded by the resolved runners trigger divided by an ambient ratio sourced from recorded context_tokens at a high quantile with its sample count recorded and a configured maximum above the resolved trigger fails a check and a lane can no longer move the bound by rewriting its own scope declaration
payload.description:
## Context

Second-order half of basicly-23ep, split out so the window fix does not carry it. **Blocked on
basicly-23ep**: calibrating a band against a finalize trigger that is itself wrong by 5x fits the
error rather than removing it.

`decompose.py:792` states the relationship: the band compares against `working_set_max`, **a
context-window ceiling**. So `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` and `supervise.ceiling_tokens` are the same
quantity and must not disagree. Two problems survive the window fix.

**1. The band gates on a proxy measured 3.16x to 7.21x low.** The band does not gate on occupancy; it
gates on `seed x scope_read_cost`. Seven paired records:

| lane | forecast_tokens | context_tokens | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| basicly-vkh0.10 | 26780 | 193096 | 7.21 |
| basicly-jr0l.64 | 34780 | 170530 | 4.90 |
| basicly-8ry8 | 18780 | 80211 | 4.27 |
| basicly-tcmy.6 | 50780 | 190177 | 3.75 |
| basicly-tcmy.22 | 49716 | 171029 | 3.44 |
| basicly-tcmy.5 | 66780 | 223221 | 3.34 |
| basicly-gczc | 66780 | 210721 | 3.16 |

A lane admitted at the band maximum of 132000 therefore lands near 495000 at the median ratio and
near 950000 at the worst - inside a corrected 600000 trigger at the median, over it at the tail.

**2. The maximum was derived from its own estimator's output.** `config.py:455-466` records that
132000 was licensed by one lane completing at that declared size, and
`run_record.py:164-171` records why that could not be checked at the time: **no field measured the
quantity the band is denominated in**, so the value was derived twice (basicly-3w44,
basicly-ipx2) by re-reading the tree and re-applying the formula to itself. `context_tokens` now
exists and carries the seven samples above, so the derivation can be replaced by a measurement for
the first time. This also subsumes **basicly-qorx's ratchet half**: once the bound stops being a
function of the largest completed self-declared scope, a lane can no longer move a global constant by
editing its own bead.

## Fix shape

**Do not hand-derive a new constant and do not fit a calibration on the proxy alone** - that is how
basicly-z2wi reached 216.65 against a seed of 3.0.

- Bound the admitted band by the resolved runner's trigger: the maximum in force for a pass is
  `min(working_set_max, ceiling_tokens(spec, sizing) / ambient_ratio)`, so it is a function of the
  runner rather than a constant that can disagree with it. A configured maximum above the resolved
  trigger is a configuration contradiction and must fail a check, the stance `config.py:831` already
  takes on `working_set_min >= working_set_max`.
- Source the ambient ratio from recorded `context_tokens` at a high quantile, matching
  basicly-jr0l.58's stance for the unsized-lane bound at `DEFAULT_UNSIZED_LANE_QUANTILE = 0.9`, and
  record the sample count so a seed reads as a seed. Seven samples is below
  `DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 10`, so the honest first landing is a **declared seed ratio with
  the gate wired**, replaced by the measured quantile once the sample crosses the minimum. State
  which of the two shipped.

Pair with basicly-jr0l.54 (verify the declared scope at landing rather than trusting it at decompose)
- an accurate ratio is meaningless if the declaration it divides is unverified.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Eighth pair, and it widens the tail (2026-08-04)

`basicly-23ep`'s own lane adds a pair that lies **outside** the range this bead was filed on:
forecast **31688**, recorded occupancy **403051** - a ratio of **12.72**, against the 3.16-7.21 the
first seven samples showed. So the tail is materially worse than the seven-sample view, and the
median is the wrong statistic to bound a ceiling with.

Two consequences for the fix:

- **A high quantile is not optional.** At 12.72x a lane admitted at the 132000 band maximum would
  occupy ~1.68M tokens - over the corrected 600000 trigger and over the 1000000 window itself. Bound
  on the observed maximum or a 0.9-plus quantile, per basicly-jr0l.58's stance, never the median.
- **The sample is now eight, still below `DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 10`.** Ship the declared
  seed with the gate wired and record it as seeded; do not fit on eight.

Worth noting *why* this lane ran so much larger than its declaration predicted: it was driven
single-track, where the ceiling turned out to be inert (basicly-7kxq), so nothing bounded it at all.
A ratio measured on an unbounded run is the honest input for a ceiling, but it is not
interchangeable with one measured on a run the finalize protocol was policing - record which each
sample is.

## Ninth pair corrects the eighth (2026-08-04)

`basicly-7kxq`: forecast **26780**, occupancy **128113** - a ratio of **4.79**, back inside the
original 3.16-7.21 band. So the note above overstated the case: **12.72 is one outlier across nine
pairs, not a new tail**, and the honest summary is a range of 3.16-12.72 with a single point above
7.3. Bound on a high quantile of the nine rather than on the maximum, and say which.

The outlier has a plausible cause worth recording rather than smoothing away: `basicly-23ep` ran on
the single-track path while the ceiling was inert there (basicly-7kxq, now closed), so **nothing
bounded it**. `7kxq` itself ran on that same path *before* its own fix landed, so it too was
unbounded - and still came in at 4.79. Two unbounded runs 2.7x apart says the spread is work-shaped,
not guard-shaped. Keep recording whether each sample ran bounded or unbounded; with the meter now
wired on both paths every future sample is bounded, which changes what the population means.
payload.title: Calibrate the working set band against measured occupancy instead of its own estimator

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 6 (D5/D6 convergence). basicly's context contribution is static projection; the "I don't know" contract is soft prose in the knowledge-priming/decision-protocol fragments the model may ignore. The loop owns a hard block-and-resume outcome (`_blocked` in loop.py) but it fires only on runner failure/checkpoints/gates, never on the agent itself signalling "iteration budget spent, fact not found".

Make a structured needs-input / I-don't-know a first-class loop outcome the HEADLESS runner can signal, mapping to the loop's existing block-and-resume contract (`_blocked(..., needs_input=<fact>)`) so the loop blocks and surfaces the missing fact instead of landing a confident wrong answer.

Signal carrier (decided): a self-ignored sentinel file the agent writes into its worktree, `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` = {"fact": ..., "detail": ...}. The loop reads it after a clean (exit 0) dispatch, blocks with needs_input, and consumes it. Robust against output redaction/truncation and agent-neutral. The manual/handoff runner is unchanged (the driver already surfaces missing facts); a manual-driver CLI is explicitly out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A headless dispatch that finishes exit 0 with a valid `.basicly/usage/needs-input.json` in the worktree blocks the loop with a needs-input result (populated `needs_input`), does NOT land the worktree, and consumes (removes) the sentinel so a re-dispatch starts clean.
- A malformed or empty sentinel is tolerated (no crash) and falls through to the normal "finished; advance again to land it" block; a missing sentinel keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- The dispatch prompt and a projected catalog fragment document the protocol (when to write the sentinel and its shape), turning the prose escalation policy into an enforced seam.
- The needs-input reason/fact is surfaced by `loop status` / advance output the same way other blocks are.
- Full suite, ruff, ruff format, pyright, bandit, and projection gates (basicly check / skills-check / agents-check / hooks-check) pass; verified by exercising a real dispatch (not just unit tests).

## Notes

- Scope is the headless dispatch path in `loop._dispatch_runner`; the sentinel lives in the already self-ignored `.basicly/usage/` dir (same convention as run-records, tool-usage, checkpoint-confirms).
payload.title: Retrieval: structured I-dont-know / needs-input as a first-class loop outcome

payload.description:
br 0.2.19 rejects the harness verify-gate call: 'br gate report <id> --gate verify --provider by-hand --status pass' fails with 'no configured transition from open requires gate verify; add a workflow.gates rule'. Reproduced on origin/main a2cdf23, so it predates the privacy-hardening work and is a tracker-version regression, not a code change.

IMPACT, two levels. Tests: 4 integration tests in tests/test_integration_loop.py fail, which blocks every push because pre-push runs the full-mode verify checks including pytest. CI never caught it because CI does not install br, so all 14 needs_br tests skip there - the gate only fires on a developer machine. Engine: verify.report_gate uses try_run_br and degrades gracefully, so the loop does not crash - it silently stops recording the verify gate. That silent degradation is arguably worse than the test failure and is the part to fix deliberately.

WHAT IS KNOWN about the policy shape, established empirically: it lives in .beads/policy.yaml, not .beads/config.yaml; workflow.gates is a map, not a sequence; its values must be a struct GateRule (serde error: 'invalid type: sequence, expected struct GateRule'); unknown fields are ignored rather than rejected, so a wrong field name parses and still fails validation. Roughly 17 candidate shapes were tried (keys: target status, gate name, from->to string; fields: require, required, requires, gates, all_of, any_of, require_all, required_gates, gate) and none satisfied validation. Passing --to explicitly does not help: --to closed and --to in_progress both fail with 'workflow does not require gate verify for transition'.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A CONFIG LINE: GateRule is documented nowhere reachable - not br robot-docs guide, not br capabilities, not br schema (which exposes no gate or workflow schema). The obvious next step, reading the beads_rust implementation, is barred by the clean-room boundary recorded in docs/design/work-tracker.md section 7: that licence is MIT with a rider naming analyzing as restricted use for this class of user. So resolving this needs the sanctioned MIT upstream gastownhall/beads, upstream docs, or a design decision instead.

payload.text:
CORRECTION + resolution (2026-07-29).

The original diagnosis was wrong on one point: CI *does* install br. quality-gates.yml:105
runs .scripts/install_br.py, and all 14 needs_br tests run there. CI stayed green because it
installs the *pinned 0.2.16*, while this machine had drifted to 0.2.19 (installed 2026-07-28
11:16 into ~/AppData/Local/Programs/br). Same commit, same test file, only the binary differs:

  br 0.2.19  ->  4 failed, 10 passed
  br 0.2.16  -> 14 passed

Reproduced outside the harness in a throwaway repo: 0.2.16 records the gate, 0.2.19 answers
'no configured transition from open requires gate verify' and exits 4. Note we ship no
.beads/policy.yaml at all, so this is 0.2.19's *default* behaviour, not a strict-policy opt-in.

CHOSEN: option (b) pin, plus option (d) fail loudly. Not (a): upgrading forward is foreclosed
by beads_rust#398 - current main targets schema 17 and its reviewed migration accepts only
13->17 and 14->17. Our .beads/beads.db is at user_version 16, outside that matrix. Verified on
a COPY that 0.2.16 reads the schema-16 DB (424 issues), records the gate, creates issues, and
leaves user_version at 16 - the downgrade is safe in both directions.

Shipped:
- br.PINNED_VERSION is now the single source; .scripts/install_br.py imports it, and the probe
  warns on ANY difference from the pin, not just below a major.minor floor.
- loop.py no longer discards report_gate's verdict. It blocked nothing before: derive_phase
  keys off gates.can_advance, so a refused gate derived back to build and advance re-ran
  build->verify forever, silently.
- .beads/.gitignore gains *-fsqlite-* - 0.2.19 writes beads.db-fsqlite-ns-{gate,use}, which
  the existing *.fsqlite-* glob misses.

LEAD for anyone who retries the policy schema: beads_rust#399's repro shows workflow.transitions
is a 'from: [to,...]' map with an 'initial:' key, per-transition gates are keyed 'in_review ->
closed' WITH SPACES around the arrow, and a TRANSITION_ANY_FROM ('any') exists. The 17 shapes
tried here used an unspaced 'from->to'. Untested - recorded only so the next attempt starts
further along.

Related upstream, neither of them this bug: #399 (br close skips validate_transition - too
permissive, opposite direction) and #398 (schema 15/16 cannot migrate to 17).

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 on the `basicly-u6jq.1` proof run: a three-lane supervised pass over
`basicly-ky5z`, `basicly-1piy` and `basicly-3ymj`, whose declared scopes are disjoint —
`src/basicly/schema.py`, `src/basicly/config.py`, `src/basicly/usage.py` and their tests.
`loop preflight` reported all three `in band` and `VERDICT: ready`.

Observed — two lanes landed, and the third could not:

```
routed:  basicly-3ymj -> bounced - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto main
         hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 1/2)
routed:  basicly-3ymj -> decision - merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-3ymj onto main
         hit conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md (rework 2/2)
blocked: 1 decision(s) await a human
```

Expected — a pass whose lanes declare disjoint scopes does not serialise on an undeclared
file, and does not spend a rework budget discovering that it does.

## Cause: every lane writes a file no lane declares

`CHANGELOG.md` is written by essentially every code lane in this repo — the landing
convention expects a `[Unreleased]` entry — and it appears in **no** bead's `## Scope`. So it
is invisible to `decompose`'s grouping and to the band table, and three lanes each inserted an
entry at the same `### Fixed` anchor. The first two landed; the third rebased onto a `main`
whose anchor had moved twice and conflicted.

The mechanism is already documented and was already known. The `harness-loop` skill's
decompose row says a plan should list in `shared` any literal path from a child's scope that
the child only *appends its own entry to* — "a manifest, a lockfile" — "otherwise that one
path serializes every child that declares it". `CHANGELOG.md` is exactly that shape, and the
rule cannot fire for it because **it is not in any scope to begin with**. `shared` can only
de-conflict a path a child declares.

Aggravating factor recorded honestly: the driving session also curated `[Unreleased]` in the
base checkout between the pass being planned and the lanes landing, which moved the anchor a
second time. That was avoidable, but it is not the root cause — three lanes appending to one
anchor collide regardless.

## Why this is not the `qorx` defect

`basicly-qorx` fixed a *tracker* gate charging siblings for one lane's declaration. This is a
*git* conflict on a real shared file, and bouncing to the lane is correct behaviour. What is
wrong is that the collision was undetectable in advance while being entirely predictable.

## Fix shape

Two halves, and the first is nearly free:

- **Declare the convention-shared paths once, in config, not per bead.** A
  `[worktree] shared_paths` (or `[loop] append_only_paths`) list naming `CHANGELOG.md`, fed
  into the same grouping `shared` already feeds, so the sizer serialises lanes that would
  collide on it instead of discovering the collision in the merge queue. A per-bead
  declaration cannot work for a path every bead touches and no bead mentions.
- **Report it in `preflight`.** The band table already names a path that collapsed the
  grouping; it should also warn when a pass of N lanes will contend on a known append-only
  path, because that is the one collision knowable before any lane starts.

Deliberately **not** proposed: teaching the merge queue to auto-resolve a `CHANGELOG.md`
conflict. A union merge of two prose entries produces text nobody reviewed, and the entry is
consumer-facing release copy.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`

- When a suppression entry names a file and a line, then that citation resolves to the suppressed condition.

- When the surface-word concept is searched, then one definition remains.

- `pyproject.toml`
- `.ruff.toml`
- `src/basicly/tracker_surface.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_invocation.py`

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a team installs only the tracker kit and lands branches for a year, I want their shards folded into the trunk without anyone running a command, so I can keep the merge promise from decaying into a directory nobody can git add.

Sharding landed in basicly-v5zvsh1 and the engine got its automatic compaction in basicly-62gd7je. A consumer with no engine has neither: compact is a command someone must remember, and fsck only warns above 1000 shards, so the first alarm comes about a year in. Measured on this repository, 8.2 merges a day is 3000 shards a year, and one git add over 10000 files costs 35.59s on NTFS against 0.66s on ext4 with the ratio doubling every decade.

Measured 2026-09-18 rather than recalled: a post-merge hook fires on a fast-forward pull and on a no-fast-forward merge, both. So a developer pulling the trunk after someone else's branch landed is exactly the moment the shard becomes foldable, and the hook is the right one.

Two problems the tier kit's hook installer did not face. A repository may point core.hooksPath somewhere other than .git/hooks, and writing the wrong place would leave a hook nothing runs. And a hook file may already exist and belong to pre-commit or husky, so it must be merged into rather than clobbered.
payload.requirements: no engine import, standard library only, no subprocess, Python 3.9 floor. The hook body carries no absolute path, no username and no bare python3, because a bare python3 on Windows hits an execution alias. core.hooksPath is read from .git/config as a file, which is the same boundary SPEC section 4.0 already amended for .git/HEAD.

## Trigger

When `skills-check` tells a consumer to move an unmanaged skill into `.basicly/core/skills/`, a path that `install` overwrites wholesale, I want a durable overlay location for a consumer's own skill, so I can keep it across an upgrade.

## Context

skills-check flags an unmanaged skill and tells the consumer to move it into .basicly/core/skills/<slug>/skill.yaml, but .basicly/core is managed and install replaces it wholesale, so anything put there is destroyed on the next upgrade. The config paths schema accepts core_fragments, overlay_fragments, targets, templates and manifest - there is no overlay_skills. So the advice the tool gives leads to silent loss, and a consumer with a skill they need has nowhere to put it. Reported by a canary who deleted theirs rather than lose it.

An install or upgrade shall not delete a skill placed in the overlay location.

payload.description:
## Context

Found and asserted by `basicly-svct4w` while fixing the opposite direction, and left as the exact mirror
of it.

`provenance.fold_edges` required `target`/`edge_type` while the engine writes `from`/`to`/`type`; that is
now fixed and reads both. **`differential.views_from_events` has the same defect the other way round**:
on a fixture holding 4 edges in the declared spelling it reads **1**.

Latent only because nothing writes the declared spelling today. It is asserted in that lane's test so it
cannot be forgotten, and it becomes live the moment any producer emits the declared pair - including a
foreign board producer, which is the whole point of the `harness-board/v1` contract.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a ledger fixture holding four edge events in the declared `target`/`edge_type` spelling.
2. Call `differential.views_from_events` over it.
3. Observe it reads one edge rather than four.
4. Call it over the same fixture written in the engine's `from`/`to`/`type` spelling and observe all four, which is the positive control.
5. Observe `provenance.fold_edges` now reads both spellings, so the two folds disagree about the same input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ledger holding edges in either spelling when the differential fold reads it then it counts every edge and reports which dialect it saw - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py -k dialect -q`
- Given a payload in neither spelling then it is still refused rather than silently dropped

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py`

## Working Set

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the differential fold is blind to the declared edge dialect the mirror of the fold just fixed

payload.text:
Closed by the commit above. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4480 tests.

The split had to come first: differential.py sat at 11110 tokens, exactly its frozen baseline, so not one line could be added. Three modules now, with the one-way direction of both seams CHECKED by a cross-reference scan rather than assumed - the derivation half takes nothing from the half it left.

  differential.py  11110 -> 8309   headroom 0 -> 2801
  derivation.py       new 3597     headroom      403
  views.py            new 1236     headroom     2764

CORRECTION to this record's number, and it cuts both ways. It says the fold reads 1 of 4. On an all-declared fixture it reads 0, measured with the engine spelling as a positive control which reads 4. The 1 is right about the fixture it came from - test_a_ledger_in_both_dialects_folds_both_and_says_which_it_read holds three declared edges and one engine edge - so both numbers are true of their own input. 0 is what a reader matching neither key returns, which is the same total blindness provenance.fold_edges had before svct4w.

The pair table is read out of provenance rather than respelled. A second copy is exactly how the two folds came to read different populations of one log, so a by-path sibling loader was cheaper than the duplication. edge_dialects reports which spellings a log carries, for EdgeFold.dialects' reason.

The test that pinned this is now the control. It asserted the 1 deliberately and its docstring said the asymmetry belonged to the other module; it now asserts equality with edge_fold.edges and compares the dialect reports, so a reader that SWITCHED spellings rather than accepting both still fails.

Two deviations. The dialect tests went to tests/test_kit_tracker_differential_probe.py, not the file the acceptance check names: that module has 16 tokens of headroom. The -k dialect selector works in the sibling. And two density waivers were taken, the same mechanism as basicly-y754k2 in this same pass - filed as basicly-e2r08j rather than absorbed a second time.

Mid-fix, my own docstring rewrite pushed tests/test_kit_tracker_provenance.py 52 tokens over its frozen 9217, which had 4 tokens of headroom. Compressed to 9208. That is basicly-e2r08j's missing instrument in one line: nothing warned me the file was at 99.96 percent of its limit.
