payload.description:
Companion of basicly-prmfjsp. Revision 2 of design version 8, written from the round-1 findings; not yet graded. Round 2 lenses: architecture, poka-yoke, recovery, tests, security, simplicity.

## Work tracker, design version 8, revision 2 (family `git-budget`)

Base: design version 7 ("v7", record basicly-gtb19bg.60). Measured facts: verify/RESULTS.md. Every command is `basicly-tracker` (packages/basicly-tracker/pyproject.toml:13).

Bad news first.

- Comments and fields reach others after p50 109 s, p95 218 s at 13 machines (measured with timer sharing; quiet sessions here wait longer).
- Five or more claims in one second can take over 10 s (measured: 9 of 13, maximum 26.5 s).
- Claims are not budgeted: 52 sessions claiming every 8.7 minutes alone reach 6 pushes per minute (arithmetic).
- A 1,000,000-event project needs 0.5 to 0.7 GB (measured), so Bitbucket Free (1 GB per workspace, sourced) holds about one.
- A 10-year vault clones in about 102 s at 10 Mbit/s (arithmetic), over S8's 60 s.

### 1. Decisions

#### 1.1 Owner decisions, each with a recommended answer

- **O1, "shared in time" (N4).** Claim, take and unassign: settled within 10 s at p99 in steady state, and always answered within 30 s. Other events: at the first command or hook after the bulk interval T (section 3.3): 60 to 72 s up to 4 active machines, 234 s at 13. S6 is not met.
- **O2, identity binding (X2).** Deferred; SSH signing prompted on Linux (measured, verify-service C5). `fsck` reports a writer id pushing under a new commit author.
- **O3, erasure (X5).** Not built. Names and emails live only in registry `person` events; events carry the person id. Erasure would be an owner-run registry rewrite with an `erasure` stub, accepted per clone by `fsck --accept-rewrite <head> --erasure <stub-id>`.
- **O4, forecast (V6) against the SPEC.md:741 non-goal.** Drop "estimate" from the non-goal: the binding board question "when will the work be done" (requirements-r1.md:28) needs it. Computed at read time; stores nothing.
- **O5, the commit hook refuses a commit with no record id.** Yes. This reverses v7 sections 8 and 9. It checks only for an id or `Record: none`, never status.

#### 1.2 Where the four designs disagreed

- **Order**: `ord` in each line (portable-core), checked along first-parent history (the other three); exports keep order and a sequencer could stamp `ord` later.
- **Registry**: one event log in vault format (evolve-v7, portable-core). **Vault scope**: one per project (budget is per repository).
- **Push at once**: claim, take, unassign, handover, project register. Not close, create or edge (git-native).
- **Bulk rule**: the simulated rule (sim.py:144-146); the others are unmeasured.
- **Commit hook**: refuse a missing id, warn on an unheld record (between evolve-v7 and portable-core).
- **Misses and links**: stored events (evolve-v7, first-principles). **PR check**: no token; id shape only. **Rotation**: by size, not year.

Dropped: stripes, the HTTP adapter, a committed STATUS.md.

#### 1.3 SPEC.md rules that a vault retires or changes

For a vault, FORMAT.md replaces these rules; the in-repository ledger keeps them until cutover.

| SPEC.md rule | In a vault |
| --- | --- |
| 4.0 `pending-<writer>` shards, `merge=union`, `compact` | Retired. One segment set per writer; nothing is compacted. |
| 4.1 per-item `seq`, sort by `seq` | Retired. One order rule: `ord` along the first-parent chain. Imported `seq` is kept in `payload.legacy_seq`. |
| 4.1 forks, `resolve`, `acknowledge-loss` | Retired. Holder verdicts decide; lost lines are re-queued by `fsck --repair`. |
| 4.5 "no format version event" | Changed. Every line carries `v`. |
| 4.6 `totals` on each event | Retired. Totals are computed by the fold. |
| Event fields `id`, `record`, `kind`, `actor`, `ts`, `payload` | Kept with the same names. Added: `v`, `ord`, `project`, `writer`, `session`, `via`. |

### 2. Data

#### 2.1 Layer map

| Layer | Contents | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kit (pure) | format, seal check, fold, holder verdicts, config fold, budget arithmetic, portfolio fold | standard library only; no network, no subprocess, no environment |
| Transport | `git_runner.py` (the only subprocess), clone, fetch, share, claim deadline, code-history reader | kit |
| Adapters | `basicly-tracker` CLI, commit hook, agent hooks, board, CI template | transport, kit |

Only adapters read environment variables. Reads never wait on the network (section 3.6).

#### 2.2 Repositories and configuration

- **Registry**: one repository per tracker; it holds every prefix, so prefixes are unique. Events: `registry-created`, `person`, `project-register`, `prefix-alias`, `project-archive`, `project-remove`, `vault-moved`, `registry-moved`, `code-location`.
- **Vault**: one repository per project, the unit of read access.
- **Both** hold `vault.toml`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py`, `README.md` (what it is, how to read and delete it) and `log/`. `vault.toml` is written once: own uid, kind, registry uid, project uid.
- **Configuration is events**: `config` events set bulk constants, minimum tool version, stale times, statuses and fields; an old event keeps the meaning in force at its `ord` (P5).
- **Code repository**: `.basicly/tracker.toml` (registry uid and URL, project uid) and one README line (C2).
- **Machine**: a user state folder (mode 0700; on Windows, `icacls` grants only the current user). Per vault: `clone/` (a bare clone, no working tree), `queue.jsonl` beside it, `sessions.json` (last activity per local session) and `log/`.

#### 2.3 Ids

- Registry, vault, project, writer and person ids: random 128-bit. None contains a host (P2, P4).
- Writer id: one per clone. Holder: (writer id, session id).
- Session id: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; or `BASICLY_TRACKER_SESSION` set from `basicly-tracker session new` (Codex, Copilot, scripts); or, for a person, one stable person session per machine, made at `attach` (D3).
- Event id: writer id plus 128 random bits, fixed at queue time. `link`, `miss` and `claim-lost` ids are content hashes, so observers agree.
- Record id: `<prefix>-<root>.<n>` (SPEC.md 9.4). A rename adds an alias; the old prefix stays owned (P3).

#### 2.4 Files and rotation

Layout: `log/<writer-id>/<nnnnn>.jsonl`; the first line of each segment is the writer header. A new segment starts at 1.5 MB: files of 1.39 MB cost 640 B per event, files of 7.3 MB cost 3.3 KB (measured, normal repack, verify/storage). 1,000,000 events at 1.39 KB raw make about 930 segments plus one open segment per writer (arithmetic; T-storage decides).

#### 2.5 Event format and seals

```text
{"v":1,"ord":8812,"id":"…","ts":"2026-11-11T09:00:00Z","project":"…","record":"abc-k3x9.2",
 "kind":"claim","writer":"…","session":"…","via":"agent","actor":"<person id>","payload":{}}
```

- Every release reads every earlier `v` (L1). `ts` is UTC RFC 3339, evidence only (L6). `actor` is the responsible person, `via` is `person` or `agent` (D4).
- Unknown kinds and fields are kept and skipped. A kind that changes holders or status carries `"fold":true`. An old tool that meets an unknown `fold` kind on a record shows the record as "needs a newer version" and refuses holder commands on it, naming the upgrade command (A1).
- Each batch ends with one seal: `{"v":1,"kind":"seal","ord":[a,b],"prev":<hash>,"hash":sha256(prev + event line bytes),"tool":"<version>"}`. The first `prev` is `sha256(vault uid)`.

**Validity.** A clone reads commits in first-parent order, taking each batch's bytes from the commit that added them. A commit is valid only when:

1. It has exactly one parent.
2. It only appends lines to one segment of one writer, and the header names that writer.
3. The lines end with one seal whose `prev` is the hash of the last valid seal.
4. The seal's range starts at the last valid end plus 1, its length equals the number of event lines, and each line carries its `ord` in sequence.
5. The hash matches.

An invalid commit (for example a web edit of an old line) is quarantined alone and reported; the next commit is judged against the same last valid seal. A forged seal with a large `ord` fails rule 4 and voids nothing else.

**Never retract.** A clone stores its last seen tip. If the new head's first-parent chain does not contain that tip (a force-push, or a bypass merge whose first parent is another branch), the clone refuses to share and names `basicly-tracker fsck --repair`.

**Repair.** `fsck --repair` re-queues every sealed line this clone saw that is not valid on the head, from any writer, with its original id; ids dedupe across repairing clones. A re-queued claim that now loses gets a `claim-lost` event, shown to the holder at the next hook and command.

**Files only.** An export holds only the valid chain. In a raw copy, a reader follows `prev` from the genesis hash, skips a batch whose hash fails, and skips seals that a `seal-void` event (written by `fsck --repair`) names.

### 3. Write, share and read

#### 3.1 Write

A command redacts secrets and absolute paths (X4), appends the event to `queue.jsonl` under `LedgerLock`, and prints one line:

- `shared` when the push landed;
- `queued; shares at your next tracker command or agent hook after <time>`, with the queue age.

With `CI` or `BASICLY_TRACKER_EPHEMERAL` set, every write shares at once. The Stop and SessionEnd hooks (SessionEnd behaviour assumed, probed by P-session) and `detach` share the whole queue.

#### 3.2 Share

Under the share lock, plumbing only:

1. Fetch. Apply the validity and never-retract rules.
2. Drop queued events whose ids are valid on the head.
3. Stamp the queued events from the last valid end plus 1 and add a seal.
4. Build the blob (head blob plus new lines) with `hash-object`, then a temporary index, `write-tree` and `commit-tree` on the head. A crash leaves only unreferenced objects.
5. Push plainly. On refusal, discard the stamps and go to step 1, at most 5 times.
6. On success, record the last seen tip, then remove the shared events from the queue under `LedgerLock`.

A share sends the events queued when it started plus one more pass (v7 drain bound).

#### 3.3 Push budget

- **Urgent**: claim, take, unassign, handover, project register. They push at once and carry the whole queue.
- **Bulk**: all others. They ride on any urgent push, or share at the first trigger after `T = max(60 s, M × 60 / 4)` times a random 0.8 to 1.2. M is the number of writers with a commit in the last hour. The constants are `config` events.
- **Triggers**: every command, every agent hook, the code pre-push hook, the board every 30 s.
- **Bursts**: one clone per machine puts all its sessions' claims into one push; nothing more is promised.

#### 3.4 Claim protocol

`basicly-tracker claim <id>` has one 30 s deadline; each git call gets only the time that remains.

1. Validate the id and session id. Missing: exit 1.
2. `git ls-remote` (at most 5 s). No answer: exit 5; nothing is queued.
3. Fetch and fold. Held by this session: exit 7. Held by another session: exit 3, with no push.
4. Append the claim to the queue.
5. Share. Another session on this machine may push it instead; that counts the same.
6. When the claim's id is valid on the head, fold. Valid: exit 0. Void (another claim came first, also in the same batch): exit 3.
7. Deadline: exit 4, "unsettled: do not start work; run basicly-tracker claim <id> --wait, or --cancel".

An unsettled claim is never treated as held; the next command or hook retries it. `claim <id> --cancel` removes it from the queue, or, if it already landed, appends an unassign. An unsettled claim older than 10 minutes is dropped with a notice, unless `--wait` renewed it.

Exit codes for every command, each with its next command:

- 0 done.
- 1 refused by name: the exact fix.
- 2 usage (argparse): `basicly-tracker <command> --help`.
- 3 held by another session: `claim <id> --take --reason "<text>"` when stale.
- 4 unsettled: `claim <id> --wait` or `--cancel`.
- 5 offline: `git ls-remote <url>`, then retry.
- 6 internal error, no traceback: `basicly-tracker doctor`; log path.
- 7 already held by this session.

#### 3.5 Other holder commands

- `claim <id> --take --reason <text>`: refused on a claim that is not stale, unless `--force`; logged; the old holder sees "taken by <name>: <reason>" at the next hook and command.
- `unassign <id>`: valid only from the holder (fixes basicly-qtmesvv).
- `handover <id> --to <holder>`: refuses a holder that never wrote to this vault, unless `--to-new`.
- `resume <old-session>`: takes back a same-writer session's claims after `/clear`; refused when `sessions.json` shows its activity in the last 30 minutes, unless `--force`; logged (D2).

#### 3.6 Read

A read serves the local fold (first valid claim by `ord` wins) and prints freshness: fetch age, last shared event per writer, queued count and age (V5). It never waits on the network (S2, D6). Fetches happen in shares, agent hooks (3 s deadline, at most once per 20 s), the pre-push hook, the board timer, `basicly-tracker sync`, and `--fresh` on any read. All worktrees on a machine share one clone and queue (D1). 13 clones fetching every 20 s make 0.65 reads per second; GitHub recommends at most 15 (sourced).

### 4. Many projects

- **Registry**: `basicly-tracker registry init <url>` initializes an empty repository. `registry move <new-url>` uses the move protocol (section 8).
- **Members**: `member add <name>` appends a `person` event; `member list`. `attach` finds the registry in `tracker.toml`; `attach --as <person-id>` links the machine user.
- **Register**: `project add --name N --prefix P --vault <url> --code <url> [--hidden]`.
  - Refuses a vault URL equal to the code URL, and a non-empty vault that is not this project's own partial one.
  - Pushes `project-register` like a claim (exit 0, 3 or 4). Until it settles, `create` under the prefix refuses. A second registration of a prefix is void and refused with the owner (P1).
  - Then initializes the vault. A rerun finds each finished step and continues.
  - Probes the vault, the code repository and the registry with anonymous `git ls-remote`. It refuses a vault more readable than its code (X1), and a vault less readable than the registry unless `--hidden`. A hidden project stores no name and no vault URL in the registry. The probe is assumed until its real-host test passes.
- **Archive and remove**: `project archive` and `project restore`. `project remove <prefix>` exports the vault, appends `project-remove`, prints the code PR file list and the forge archive step, and resumes (A4).
- **Portfolio**: folds every cloned vault; one with no access shows "no access".
- **Dependencies**: an edge stores the full target id; without access it shows "hidden record".

### 5. Never forget

Code never changes a status. Each point refuses a missing link or reports it.

- **Commit-msg hook** (installed by `attach`, version-marked). Refuses a commit with no record id and no `Record: none`; fills in ` (<id>)` when the session holds exactly one claim; warns with the claim command when the record is not held or is unsettled (V4); offline, passes and records a local miss. Cannot catch: `--no-verify`, a machine without `attach`, forge-side commits.
- **Agent hooks** (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd). Show held, stale, unsettled and lost claims, suggestions and queued events; fetch; share. Cannot catch: a person with no agent.
- **PR check** (CI template, no token). Refuses a PR with no id shape and no `none`, and a changed project uid. Advisory where it cannot be a required check (GitHub Free private repositories; Bitbucket without Premium).
- **Audit in session start and every share** (`fsck --code`, on the local code clone). Lists suggestions from `closes <id>` and reverts, merged commits with no record, every `Record: none` commit, in-progress records with no code activity, and stale claims. Stores `link` and `miss` events (V3, L5).

What slips past: a bypassed commit shows as a `miss` at the next audit; a quiet session shows an old "last shared" time; an unsettled claim elsewhere is invisible until it lands.

### 6. Visibility

- **Portfolio** (`basicly-tracker portfolio`, board): per project, holders, blocked, stale claims, ready count, closed in 7 days, misses, forecast, freshness (V1). The board fetches vaults in parallel.
- **Stale claims**: no event or linked commit by the holder for 2 hours (agent) or 3 days (person), configurable, assumed. Flagged with holder and age, never released (V2).
- **Forecast**: a range from closed events per week, with sample size (after O4).
- **After /clear**: SessionStart lists other sessions' claims on this writer and prints `resume <old-session>`.
- **Output**: versioned `--json`; no prompt, editor or pager (D5, D7).

### 7. Security

- **Credentials**: the user's git credentials only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, no token written (X7). On an authentication failure `attach` prints the sign-in step.
- **Input**: `git_runner.py` validates ids and URLs (only `https`, `ssh`); hooks get paths through environment variables.
- **Redaction**: on by default on every write path (X4).
- **Untrusted text**: record text reaches an agent only between `<<<record-text` and `record-text>>>`, control characters stripped; nothing runs or follows it (X6).
- **Tamper detection**: the never-retract check, the seal rules and the writer header. Every clone reports at its next command (X3).
- **Board**: loopback only; a state change needs a per-session token and matching Host and Origin (X8).

### 8. Longevity

- **FORMAT.md** and **reader.py** (standard library, at most 300 lines) in every repository; CI checks that reader.py folds to the kit's records (L2).
- **Export**: `basicly-tracker export <dir>` writes the valid chain sorted by `ord`, `FORMAT.md`, `reader.py` and a SHA-256 manifest. `import <dir>` restores into an empty vault and checks the seals (L4). Recovery point: each writer's last share.
- **Move** (vault or registry): `basicly-tracker move <new-url>`. (1) Push a final `vault-moved` batch to the old URL; after it, every tool refuses writes there and names the new URL. (2) Copy the history to the empty target. (3) Check that the target head equals the old head. (4) Append `vault-moved` to the registry. A rerun resumes at the first unfinished step. No id changes (P4).
- **Continue**: `basicly-tracker vault continue <new-url>` ends the vault with a final seal, then starts a successor vault whose genesis `prev` is that final seal's hash. The fold reads both as one chain.
- **Growth budget**: 0.64 KB per event (measured). At an assumed 20,000 events per year, 64 MB at 5 years. `status` warns at 70 % of the host limit or the 5-year clone time and names `vault continue`.

### 9. Install, upgrade, migration, removal

- **Install**: one README line, `uv tool install git+https://github.com/<owner>/basicly@<tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`, then `basicly-tracker attach`. Each missing piece is refused with its exact command (A3). A gate checks that every documented command exists in `--help` (A7).
- **Upgrade**: `basicly-tracker upgrade` prints `uv tool install --force git+https://…@<new-tag>#subdirectory=packages/basicly-tracker`; run again after it, `upgrade` migrates state and hooks, prints both versions, resumes, and refuses a downgrade (A2).
- **Minimum version**: `upgrade --vault` raises it by a `config` event and lists the active writers not yet on it; `--force-minimum` overrides, logged; `--lower` undoes it while no event uses the new `v`.
- **Migration**: one resumable command, `basicly-tracker migrate --from ledger|beads|beans <path> --vault <url> [--preview]`. For the ledger it freezes, imports in today's fold order keeping ids, verifies count and digest, and writes the cutover files (v7 section 11). `migrate --rollback` exports post-cutover vault events into the old ledger with a digest check and unfreezes (A5).
- **Removal**: `project remove` (section 4); `basicly-tracker uninstall` per machine refuses a non-empty queue unless `--export <file>`, then removes hooks and state and lists leftovers (A4).
- **Platforms**: CI on Windows, macOS and Linux, with paths with spaces, `icacls` and PowerShell sessions (A6).

### 10. Recovery

Commands omit `basicly-tracker`. Each row Rn has a test (section 11).

- R1 crash in a share step: queue intact; only unreferenced objects. Repair: next command, or `share`.
- R2 torn queue tail: cut back under `LedgerLock`. Repair: automatic.
- R3 host outage: claims exit 5; others queue. Repair: `share` when back.
- R4 vault force-push or bypass merge: shares refuse. Repair: `fsck --repair` (any writer's lines).
- R5 registry force-push or loss: registry commands refuse. Repair: `fsck --repair --registry`, or `registry move <url>` from any clone.
- R6 vault lost on the host: any clone holds history to its last fetch. Repair: `move <new-url>` from that clone, or `import <dir>`.
- R7 lost machine: its unshared events lost; claims go stale. Repair: `claim <id> --take --reason`.
- R8 unsettled claim: queued, shown unsettled. Repair: `claim <id> --wait` or `--cancel`.
- R9 prefix race lost: registration void. Repair: `project add` with another prefix.
- R10 crash in `project add`: partial steps. Repair: rerun `project add`.
- R11 corrupt clone: `queue.jsonl` outside the clone. Repair: `reclone` (refuses with an unshared queue unless `--export`).
- R12 crash in `move`: old URL fenced. Repair: rerun `move <new-url>`.
- R13 crash in migration: resumes by event id. Repair: rerun `migrate`.
- R14 cutover regretted: vault holds new events. Repair: `migrate --rollback`.
- R15 bad release raised the minimum: writers refused. Repair: `upgrade --vault --lower`.
- R16 claim lost after repair: `claim-lost` event. Repair: shown; `claim <id>` again.

### 11. Proof tests

Local CI: bare repositories, push 1.5 s, fetch 0.5 s injected. Load tests run nightly on a dedicated runner.

**Named tests**

- T-claim-load: drives the real `claim` command end to end. 52 sessions on 13 machines, one claim per session per 20 minutes, 10 bulk events per session per hour, 6 runs of 70 minutes with seeds 1 to 6, at least 1,000 claims. Pass: p99 at most 10 s, every claim answered within 30 s, mean at most 6 push attempts per minute, busiest minute at most 18.
- T-claim-burst: 13 claims in one second, one fetch stalled: every answer within 30 s; latency reported only.
- T-exclusive: 3 clones, and 8 sessions in one clone, claim one record: exactly one exit 0.
- T-bulk: shares driven by a modelled hook schedule (one prompt per session per 2 minutes, assumed): p95 within 1.2 T plus 2 minutes.
- T-fork: property test over interleavings with bypass merges, forged seals (large `ord`, wrong length) and web edits. Pass: no seal a clone has seen is retracted, a forged batch voids only itself, and a changed verdict yields `claim-lost`.
- T-writers (S3): 16 processes on one machine plus 50 clones: every event lands once.
- T-storage (S1, L3): 50 live writers plus 200 retired writer folders, 1,000,000 events: at most 0.7 GB after a normal repack, under 1,000 files.
- T-clone5y (S8): a 5-year vault (100,000 events): pack at most 70 MB, clone within 60 s at 10 Mbit/s.
- T-flaky (S7): the remote vanishes for 10 minutes and returns: the first hook after it shares the queue once.
- T-wrong-use: one case per refusal in sections 3 to 9: exit code, named cause, next command, no state change.
- T-exit: table-driven, one case per exit code and its printed next command (D5, D7).

**Real-host probes** (sandbox GitHub and Bitbucket; owner approval needed)

- P-claim: 13 clones, 2 hours. Pass: p99 at most 10 s, mean at most 6 pushes per minute, no rate-limit error, latency at most twice an idle baseline.
- P-visibility: four public and private combinations of vault and code. Pass: every answer right within 10 s, no prompt.
- P-session: a session and its subagent see one `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; rerun on each Claude Code release.
- P-merge: two code PRs with tracker writes stay mergeable after one merges (N1).

**Traceability** (every section 6 id; "def." means deferred with its section)

| Group | Id to test |
| --- | --- |
| P | P1 T-register; P2 T-move; P3 T-prefix (race, alias); P4 T-move (GitHub to bare); P5 T-config (rename a status) |
| V | V1 T-portfolio; V2 T-stale; V3 T-audit; V4 T-hook; V5 T-fresh; V6 T-forecast after O4; V7 T-handover, notices def. (13) |
| D | D1 T-worktree; D2 T-resume; D3 P-session, T-session; D4 T-actor; D5 T-exit; D6 T-offline; D7 T-exit, T-wrong-use |
| S | S1 T-storage; S2 T-perf (10,000 records, operation counts); S3 T-writers; S4 T-claim-load; S5 T-claim-load; S6 T-bulk (not met, 13); S7 T-flaky; S8 T-clone5y, T-portfolio100 |
| X | X1 P-visibility, T-hidden; X2 def. (O2), T-author-mismatch; X3 T-fork, T-tamper; X4 T-redact; X5 def. (O3); X6 T-untrusted; X7 T-no-token; X8 T-board; X9 def. (13) |
| L | L1 T-versions; L2 T-reader; L3 T-storage; L4 T-export; L5 T-link; L6 T-ts |
| A | A1 T-mixed (old tool refuses holder commands on a `fold` kind); A2 T-upgrade (two tags, crash, downgrade); A3 T-newcomer; A4 T-remove; A5 T-migrate, T-rollback; A6 T-platform; A7 T-doctor, T-help-gate |
| R | R1 to R16: one test each injects the failure, runs the repair, and compares the fold digest with an unfailed control run |

A CI gate refuses an id with no test and no deferral.

### 12. Build slices

Slices S2 to S4 change and need new approval. Order as listed.

- S2 kit: format, seals, validity, fold by `ord`, holder verdicts, config fold (section 1.3).
- S3 transport: bare clone, queue, plumbing share, never-retract, repair, triggers. T-claim-load passes before merge.
- S4 claims: deadline, exit codes, unsettled, cancel, expiry, take, handover, resume.
- S8 registry (new): registry, members, projects, portfolio, probes.
- S5 audit: `link`, `miss`, `Record: none` as a miss.
- S6 hooks and PR check.
- S9 longevity (new): FORMAT.md, reader.py, export, import, move, continue.
- S7 migration: one `migrate` command, rollback.
- S10 lifecycle (new): upgrade, doctor, uninstall, three-platform CI.
- S11 forecast (new): after O4.

Reused: slice S1 (`git_runner.py`), `LedgerLock`, `holders.py`, `fsck.py`, `migrate.py`, `beads.py`, `beans.py`, `board.py`; `events.py` gains the vault mode.

### 13. Section 6 requirements not met

- S4: not met for 5 or more claims in one second (the header).
- S5: the busiest minute reaches 12 to 18.
- S6: not met above 4 active machines; GitHub's push guidance wins.
- S7: met only when a command or hook runs after the network returns.
- S8: met to 5 years; then `vault continue`. S1: about 1,000,000 events per vault.
- X1: partly; hidden projects still show a prefix and a uid in the registry.
- X2, X5, V6: O2, O3, O4. X9: roles are forge permissions. V7: notices need a server.

### 14. Changes from round 1

| Fix | Finding (lens) |
| --- | --- |
| 2.5 validity, never retract, `claim-lost`, `seal-void` | fork voids honest seals (architecture, poka-yoke, recovery) |
| 1.3 retired SPEC rules | two specs (architecture) |
| 2.1 layer map; 3.6 local reads | no layer map (architecture) |
| 2.2 `config` events, write-once `vault.toml` | two config mechanisms (architecture) |
| 2.2, 8 registry uid, fenced move, continue, one prefix namespace | moves and P3 (architecture, poka-yoke, recovery) |
| 2.2 `queue.jsonl` outside the clone; R11 | queue in `.git` (poka-yoke, recovery) |
| 3.4 cancel, expiry, one deadline | unsettled claims, 30 s (poka-yoke, recovery, tests) |
| 3.5 resume fence, take reason, handover check | holder misuse (poka-yoke) |
| 3.1 share at exit | throwaway environments (poka-yoke) |
| 4 `project add` refusals, rerun, `--hidden` | registration misuse (poka-yoke) |
| 2.5 `fold` marker | mixed versions (poka-yoke) |
| 5 `Record: none` is a miss | silent escape (poka-yoke) |
| 3.4, 4, 9 one executable, upgrade, member, registry, remove, migrate, Windows | operability |
| 3.2 plumbing share; 10 R1 to R16 | recovery gaps (recovery) |
| 11 traceability, R-tests, wrong use, peak minute, 5-year clone, real `claim` load | tests |

payload.text:
NEXT-SESSION PLAN (loop state machine, onb.6.3). 3rd of onb.6's four children; READY now (.1 state-model + .2 classify closed). This is the INTEGRATION HUB — it composes every module built so far. THIN CONDUCTOR: the engine advances phases + enforces gates; the AGENT supplies inputs (work type, decomposition plan) and does the actual coding in worktrees. State is read from br every time (resumable); nothing is cached.

MODULE: new src/basicly/loop.py + tests/test_loop.py.

CORE SHAPE — a single-step, resumable transition:
- advance(repo_root, issue_id, *, config=None, work_type=None, children=None) -> AdvanceResult.
- It FIRST reads loop_state.read_node_state(issue_id) to get the current phase (resume point), then dispatches on phase via a HANDLER DICT (phase -> _handler), mirroring cmd_worktree/cmd_policy dispatch so we stay under PLR0911 (<=6 returns) / PLR0913 (<=5 args) — pass agent inputs in a small frozen Inputs dataclass, not as many kwargs.
- AdvanceResult(frozen): from_phase, to_phase (== from_phase when blocked), action ("classified"/"decomposed"/"built"/"merged"/"verified"/"shipped"/"tore-down"/"blocked"/"escalated"), blocked_reason|None, needs_input|None (what the agent/human must supply next). No exceptions for normal blocks — return a blocked result.

PHASE -> ACTION MAPPING (each composes an already-tested module):
- intake: requires work_type; absent -> blocked(needs_input="work_type"); present -> classify.classify(repo,id,work_type) -> to "classify".
- classify: gated by the classify human checkpoint (policy.checkpoint_approved) AND DoR (classify returns can_leave_classify / policy.definition_of_ready). Both true -> to "decompose"; else blocked(needs classify checkpoint approval and/or DoR sections).
- decompose: requires children plan; absent -> blocked(needs_input="children"); present -> decompose.decompose(repo,id,children); then gated by the decompose checkpoint -> to "build".
- build: for each dependency-unblocked child (loop_state.ready_ranked, concurrency-capped by WorktreeConfig), worktree.create(name) and stash the binding via br update --external-ref loop_state.format_worktree_ref(name,branch). Agent builds + verifies each child (that is child-level advance recursion — see design Q3). When children are green -> to "merge".
- merge: merge.merge_queue(repo, [(name,bead)...], config) in the decomposer's serial/topological order; on a node failure the queue already records rework + escalation (policy) -> surface as blocked/escalated.
- verify: verify.run_verify(repo, mode) + verify.report_gate(repo,id,report); gate_status must show the required gate green (policy.gate_status.can_advance) -> to "ship"; fail -> policy.record_rework + should_escalate (bounded n=2, config.max_rework) -> blocked/escalated.
- ship: gated by the ship human checkpoint -> to "teardown".
- teardown: worktree.cleanup for the node's worktrees + br close the issue -> "done".

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE IN-SESSION:
(Q1) Single-step advance() core vs a run() loop. RECOMMEND: advance() is the primitive (resumable, agent/human re-invokes each step); add a thin run_until_blocked(repo, issue_id, inputs) driver that loops advance() until it blocks/checkpoints/finishes. The CLI (onb.6.4) wires both; one-shot mode (arch 12.2) = auto-approve the middle checkpoint in the driver.
(Q2) Where agent inputs live: pass work_type/children into advance() (or an Inputs dataclass); when a phase needs one and it is absent, block and report needs_input. Keeps the engine agent-agnostic (no prompting inside the engine).
(Q3) Fractal recursion (epic->feature->task, arch 12.1/12.2). RECOMMEND scope onb.6.3 to the SINGLE-TRACK linear machine; children advance via the SAME advance() invoked per child by the driver over ready_ranked. Full auto-recursion inside one advance() call is deferred (leave a clear hook + a note); the AC only requires the linear phase machine + checkpoints + rework + resume. Confirm this boundary.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When coding agents work in parallel, I want worktrees that are commissioned, used and decommissioned by one agent-agnostic process, so I can parallelize, merge and see all work safely and fast.

## Owner rules (2026-10-07)

1. Working with worktrees is agnostic of the coding agent.
2. Worktrees live in a sibling folder of the repository, at the same level as the repository folder.
3. Worktrees are never inside the repository (for example under .claude), because they interfere with the CI gates.
4. Worktrees enable a high level of parallel work.
5. A worktree is commissioned, worked in, and decommissioned (deleted and cleaned up) when its work is complete.
6. A worktree lives only until its work is merged back into the branch that created it (usually main, possibly another feature branch).
7. Worktree work is secure, stable, transparent and fast.

The harness needs solid parallelization, merging, transparency, orchestration, coordination, idempotency and agent agnosticity.

## Evidence (measured 2026-10-07)

- git worktree list: 11 live harness worktrees; git merge-base --is-ancestor shows 9 of 11 branches already merged into main and never decommissioned (rule 5, rule 6).
- basicly worktree create refused: concurrency cap reached (11/10 live), so parallel work stopped (rule 4).
- Claude Code auto-mode denied basicly worktree cleanup of two merged, clean worktrees as irreversible local destruction, so decommissioning needs a manual permission (rule 5, rule 7).
- The sibling folder is named basicly.worktrees; the owner wrote <repo>.worktree. Confirm the name (rule 2).
- Memory note: the Agent tool isolation:worktree checks out inside the repository and poisons whole-tree gates (rule 3); basicly worktree bg-isolation exists for it.
payload.requirements:
- Audit src/basicly/worktree.py, the worktree-isolation skill and the loop landing against each of the seven rules, and record a pass or fail with evidence per rule.
- Keep refusal of unmerged or dirty worktrees; never delete unmerged work.
- No dependency changes.
payload.title: Review the worktree work process against the seven owner rules

payload.text: Evidence 2026-10-07 (rule 5 and rule 7). basicly worktree cleanup refused a clean merged worktree because ignored generated caches (.pytest_cache, .ruff_cache, __pycache__) count as uncommitted changes; the only remedy offered is force, which also discards real work. 10 of 11 worktrees are merged and hold only generated leftovers (ledger redirect, .import_linter_cache, node_modules, caches), classified by git status --porcelain --ignored. The Claude Code auto-mode classifier then denied both cleanup and cleanup --force, so decommission depends on a manual permission. Fix candidates: cleanup classifies every generated leftover it or its tools create as owned and removes a merged worktree without force; the shipped Claude settings allow basicly worktree cleanup of a merged clean worktree.

[merged from basicly-jr0l.71, triage 2026-11-17] A nested node_modules and an agent worktree both poison the markdownlint gate
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a nested `node_modules` or a linked agent worktree sits inside the repository root, I want the markdownlint gate to exclude both, so I can stop a commit being blocked by errors in files this repo does not own.

## Context

Reproduced 2026-08-07 while landing `basicly-vkh0.18`. The commit was rejected by the
`markdownlint` pre-commit hook for three errors, two of them in a file this repo does not
own:

```
.claude/worktrees/agent-<id><redacted:posix-absolute-path>:1
  MD043/required-headings
.claude/worktrees/agent-<id><redacted:posix-absolute-path>:16:81
  MD013/line-length
```

Two independent defects, both in `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`:

1. `ignores: node_modules/**` is anchored at the repo root, so it does not match a
   **nested** `node_modules`. Any nested install is linted as if it were ours.
2. A linked git worktree created inside the root (`.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/`, which is
   what a parallel agent spawn creates) is inside `globs: **/*.md`, so every markdown file
   in the repo is linted twice and the worktree's own dependencies are linted at all.

## This is the class basicly-jr0l.70 fixed for one gate only

`jr0l.70` hardened `wired-or-deleted` against exactly this — a worktree inside the root
duplicating every module under a second site label. Its closing note recorded the open
question: every other whole-tree analysis can be poisoned the same way, unverified. This is
that verification, on a gate nobody had checked, and it is a **hard block on a commit**
rather than a silent miscount.

Note MD013 is `false` in this repo's config and fired anyway, because markdownlint-cli2

## Trigger

When a repository adopts the comment ban through `basicly install` it gets the always-on rule and no skill, while a standalone consumer gets a full skill, so the integrated consumer has less guidance than the standalone one.

## Measured, 2026-09-12

`ls .basicly/core/skills/ | grep -i comment` returns nothing. The catalog ships `work-tracker` and `tier-injection` for the other two kits and nothing for the comment ban. The ban's guidance for a basicly consumer is the `code-is-authoritative` rule alone, which is a paragraph; the standalone consumer gets `.basicly/core/kit/comments/GUIDANCE.md`, which says where a fact goes now that a comment cannot hold it, which comments are directives that stay, and what the three proofs mean.

A second, smaller asymmetry: `basicly install` copies `GUIDANCE.md` and `INSTRUCTION.md` into `.basicly/core/kit/<name>/` and nothing projects them, so they sit inert in every basicly consumer.

## What must not happen

Two texts saying the same thing in two places is how a claim goes stale. Whatever lands must make the kit's skill and the catalog's skill one text with a gate on it, not a copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE CATALOG SHALL carry a skill for the comment ban, so a basicly consumer is told the same thing a standalone consumer is told.
- THAT SKILL AND the kit's `GUIDANCE.md` SHALL be one text, and a gate SHALL fail where they diverge.
- THE KIT README SHALL say that `GUIDANCE.md` and `INSTRUCTION.md` are the standalone path's source and are not projected by `basicly build`, so a reader does not look for their output.
- A TEST SHALL assert the catalog skill exists, is discoverable by its description, and matches the kit text.

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: install through basicly into a throwaway repo and show the comment-ban skill where an agent reads it

payload.description:
## Context

An audit of 24 live work items on 2026-08-13 checked every `file:line` citation it relied on.
**14 of 14 had drifted.** This is one missing mechanism, not fourteen defects:

```text
runner.py:141-142        -> :151            basicly.toml:512 / :568   -> :619
supervise.py:2700        -> :2727           cli.py:3582               -> :3589
merge.py:466 / :520      -> :475 / :529     cli.py:3265               -> :3314
policy.py:560            -> :673            run_record.py:605         -> :742
supervise.py:1286        -> :1222           loop.py:327               -> moved module
supervise._band_verdict  -> working_set.py:285
```

Why it matters more than tidiness: a citation is how a work item makes its claim checkable, and
the repo's own rule is "re-check a cited `file:line` before fixing it"
(`implementation-plan.md`, section 1 item 2). When every citation is stale, that rule costs a
re-derivation per item and readers stop performing it - which is how `basicly-4xmu`'s
reproduction came to omit `_run_proposer`, and how a P0 was nearly built against a remedy the
plan had replaced.

Two live items show the failure in its worst form, where the **symbol** moved rather than the
line: `basicly-esxp` cites `supervise._band_verdict`, now `working_set.py:285`; and
`basicly-o40x`'s declared `## Scope` names `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop.skill.yaml`, a
path that **matches no file** (the real one is `harness-loop/skill.yaml`). A scope glob matching
nothing is what `basicly-a3ab.3` exists to catch for catalog entries, and nothing catches it for
a bead's own scope block - `basicly policy dor` warns only when a `## Scope` heading parsed to
zero globs, not when a declared glob matches zero files.

## Why a line number is the wrong thing to store

The durable identifier is the symbol, not the offset. A check that re-resolves
`module.function` and reports where it now lives survives every refactor; a check that compares
stored line numbers fails on the first unrelated insertion above them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick any live bead older than a week that cites a `file:line`.
2. Open the cited line. Positive control before reporting drift: confirm the file exists and the
   symbol is findable elsewhere in it, so "wrong line" is distinguishable from "deleted".
3. Observed: 14 of 14 sampled citations pointed at the wrong line or a moved module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a live work item citing a symbol that has moved, when the check runs, then it names the
  item, the stale citation and the symbol's current location - check: a test plants a bead
  citing a known-moved symbol and asserts all three appear.
- Given a work item whose declared `## Scope` carries a glob matching no file on disk, when the
  check runs, then it is named - check: `basicly-o40x` is reported today, and a corrected scope
  is not.
- Given a citation that is still correct, when the check runs, then it is silent - check: the
  false-positive case, asserted on a bead whose citation resolves.
- Given the check, when it cannot find the file at all, then it distinguishes deleted from moved
  - check: a bead citing a path removed in `28257e9` reports "deleted", not "drifted".

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_bead_citations.py` names the drifted citations across the live
tracker and exits non-zero, and `--strict` or a per-bead argument reports one item.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_bead_citations.py`
- `tests/test_check_bead_citations.py`
- `basicly.toml`

## Context

When coding agents on one machine cannot message each other directly, for example a Codex session and a Claude session, I want a catalog skill with a bundled script that gives them one shared mailbox folder and locks, so they can coordinate work without a person relaying every message. The owner asked for it: "the mail script should be a general script that all developers can use, it should create the .orchestrator local folder and add it to git ignore, in essence it should be a skill that can be invoked and used and the goal is to establish communication with the coding agents that cannot exchange messages directly."

The reference is the workspace's local bash script .orchestrator/bin/mail and its README. The new script is Python standard library only and keeps the reference's commands, exit codes and folder layout.

Root discovery, first match wins: the ORCH_MAIL_ROOT variable; an upward search from the current folder for a .orchestrator folder with the init marker; the same search from the folder above the main worktree of the current git repository. A .orchestrator folder without the marker is refused by name. No command except init creates the folder.

Fixed faults of the reference: send could overwrite a message (mv -n checks before it renames); a lock was visible before its owner was written.

To keep the Codex skill listing at or under 6762 characters (measured on 3b7beee6), this cut shortens other skill descriptions; the list and their routing results are recorded in a comment.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"even a graph on the page is a nice touch"*, in the same breath as *"is the work parallel or sequential"*.

The board cannot answer that second question and the data is already on the contract. `graph.edges` rides on every snapshot; the page draws it as **one number in the footer** — `DEP EDGES 843` — and as the feature heading on a ready row. The structure itself is never drawn.

`board_footer`'s own docstring states the intent the number falls short of: edges are *"the answer to why an item is not ready - the one question a count of blocked items raises and cannot settle"*. The page prints `BLOCKED 56` beside `DEP EDGES 843` and settles nothing.

## What a reader is asking

Not the whole graph. 843 edges over 291 active records is not a picture. The questions are:

- **is the next work parallel or sequential** — how wide is the ready frontier, and how deep is the chain behind the top of it;
- **why is this blocked** — for a named record, what holds it;
- **what unblocks the most** — which single record has the most dependents.

The third is what the scheduler already ranks on (`priority ASC, dependents DESC`), and the page never shows the second term.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the region renders, IT SHALL show the depth of the chain behind the ready frontier, so a reader can tell parallel work from a queue.
- WHEN a record is drawn anywhere on the page as blocked, THE REGION SHALL name what holds it, not merely that something does.
- WHEN one record unblocks more than any other, IT SHALL be named with its dependent count.
- WHERE the edge set is too large to draw, THE REGION SHALL state the bound it drew within and what it dropped, never a silent sample.
- WHERE `graph` is absent from the snapshot, THE REGION SHALL say so and SHALL NOT read as an unblocked backlog.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_graph.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_graph.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- demonstration: Read off the board which record unblocks the most work, and check it against `basicly tracker blocked`.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a coding agent writes code it writes prose with it, and the prose then has to be kept true as the code moves, so the owner wants comments banned from code outright, enforced deterministically rather than by guidance, so the code is the only source of truth and a change to it can never leave a stale claim behind.

## Context

Owner, 2026-09-12: "ever since watermarking has been a part of the claude models, the comments in files have blown out of proportions". The rule is that the code is the authoritative source of truth, and the benefit is that changing code no longer obliges anyone to update a comment. This inverts the repository's current position, which is encoded in the `comment-density` ratchet, the `code-is-authoritative` rule and the comment sections of `python-guidelines` - all of which argue that prose carrying a why is evidence and must stay.

## Measured, 2026-09-12

Census over the tracked tree with `tokenize` and `ast`:

| population | count | chars |
| --- | --- | --- |
| prose `#` comments | 9926 lines | 710430 |
| docstrings | 9582 | 2489642 |
| functional directives | 332 lines | - |

Directives break down as `noqa` 122, `nosec` 108, `type: ignore` 48, `comment-density-waiver:` 25, `pragma: no` 14, `module-size-waiver:` 10, shebang 2, `fmt:` 3. Every one of these is read by a tool and must survive a strip, or the build stops. Docstrings are 78% of the prose mass.

Tracked file types: 554 `.py`, 3 `.html`, 1 each of `.sh`, `.ps1`, `.mjs`, `.css`, plus 12 `.j2`. So this repository exercises mainly Python; the kit must still cover the wider set a consumer has.

## The two docstring consumers, enumerated rather than assumed

- `.scripts/docs_claims.py:205` calls `ast.get_docstring` on each hook script to fill the Description column of the generated `catalog-hooks` table in `.basicly/core/hooks/README.md`. Strip docstrings and that column empties.
- Nine `.scripts/*.py` CLIs pass `description=__doc__` to `argparse`, so `--help` comes from the module docstring.

Both need a replacement before the strip: the hook description moves into `hooks.yaml` as a real field, and `description=__doc__` becomes a string literal. A string is code, not a comment.

## Owner decisions, 2026-09-12

- Docstrings are in scope; both comments and docstrings go.
- The `comment-density` ratchet, its 25 waivers, its frozen tables and its `basicly.d` entries are deleted, along with the guidance that argues for prose.
- The gate checks in CI and in pre-commit, and strips only on an explicit `--fix`. It never rewrites behind the committer.
- Covered: all code files - Python, shell, JS/TS, HTML, CSS, Java, C# and the other .NET languages. Excluded: config files, Markdown and docs.
- Packaged as a kit and distributed by `uvx` exactly as the tier and tracker kits are: its own package, vendor-by-default `init`, also runs direct, git-only channel until the v1.0.0 freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE KIT SHALL report every comment in a code file it supports, naming the file and line.
- THE KIT SHALL remove those comments only when `--fix` is given, and SHALL leave every functional directive in place.
- THE KIT SHALL refuse a file it cannot lex confidently rather than strip it, because a wrong strip corrupts source.
- WHERE the language is Python, THE STRIP SHALL be verified by re-parsing and comparing the abstract syntax tree with docstrings removed.
- THE STRIP SHALL be idempotent: a second pass over stripped output SHALL change zero bytes.
- THE STRIP SHALL NOT alter the content of any string literal.
- THE GATE SHALL run in CI as a `[[verify.checks]]` entry and at commit time as a hook.
- THE REPOSITORY SHALL carry no prose comment or docstring in a covered file once the migration lands, and the suite, `ruff` and `pyright` SHALL stay green.
- THE RUFF CONFIGURATION SHALL NOT select a rule that requires a docstring.
- THE KIT SHALL install into a repository that never runs basicly, by `uvx`, exactly as `basicly-tracker` and `basicly-tier` do.

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- demonstration: run the kit against a throwaway repository holding one file per supported language, check it reports every comment, fix it, and confirm the files still compile and the directives survive
payload.title: ban comments in code and ship the comment strip kit

payload.value: All five stages landed across four commits. The kit (00b175e1), the two docstring consumers moved off docstrings (24319f9f), the repo-wide strip (4f6922db, 54808 deletions across 607 files), and the gate plus guidance (089c2c8e). Measured after: 0 prose comments in 570 covered files and every one of the 335 directives intact. The three proofs refused 95 files on the first run and 84 on the second and both defects were real - a blank-line pass comparing global counts positionally, then ast reporting col_offset in utf-8 bytes where tokenize reports characters. Ruff no longer selects pydocstyle. comment-density and retired-vocabulary are retired with their subject; working_set_min was recalibrated 8000 to 4600 because its unit moved 41.75 percent; module-size debt fell from 67 frozen entries to 46. no-comments now runs at pre-commit and as a verify check in fast and full.
